groups.name: Rivers, gravel bars and glacier forelands

charetea.name: Stonewort beds in still water
charetea.desc: Underwater meadows of stoneworts (Chara, Nitella) in clear, nutrient-poor, usually calcareous lakes and ponds. These algae look like tiny horsetails and often carry a crust of lime. They need very clean water and disappear quickly when nutrients rise.
charetea.sub: Corpi d'acqua ferma con vegetazione sommersa priva di piante vascolari

utricularietea.name: Natural dystrophic pools
utricularietea.desc: Small, acidic, peat-stained pools in bogs and mires. The water is poor in nutrients, so carnivorous bladderworts trap tiny animals with underwater bladders. Floating peat mosses are common. Very rare and sensitive to drainage and nutrient input.

potamion.name: Submerged pondweed communities
potamion.desc: Fully submerged plant stands in still or slow, fairly nutrient-rich water: pondweeds, water-milfoils and naiads rooted on the bottom. Found in the lowland lakes (Kalterer See, Montiggler Seen) and in old river arms and ditches.

nymphaeion.name: Rooted floating-leaved communities (water lilies)
nymphaeion.desc: Rooted plants with large leaves floating on the surface: water-lilies and floating pondweeds. Typical of sheltered bays of lowland lakes and ponds with a muddy bottom.

lemnetea.name: Free-floating duckweed communities
lemnetea.desc: Free-floating carpets of duckweeds and frogbit on calm, nutrient-rich water. They cover ponds, ditches and sheltered bays, mostly in the warm valley floors.

ranunculion.name: Flowing-water vegetation
ranunculion.desc: Vegetation of clear, flowing water: water-crowfoots, water-parsnip and bur-reeds rooted in streams and spring-fed ditches. Their long shoots stream with the current. Threatened by channel works and pollution.

bryobrooks.name: Mountain streams dominated by mosses
bryobrooks.desc: Fast, cold mountain streams where flowering plants can barely root; mosses, liverworts and aquatic lichens cover the stones instead. Indicates clean, well-oxygenated water.
bryobrooks.sub: Vegetazione dei corsi d'acqua montani, a prevalenza di briofite

adiantion.name: Tufa-forming calcareous springs and seeps
adiantion.desc: Dripping, sunny limestone walls and springs where lime precipitates from the water and builds porous tufa. Maidenhair fern grows here at its northern limit. A priority habitat under the EU Habitats Directive.
adiantion.sub: Sorgenti calcaree e stillicidi con formazione di tufi

cratoneurion.name: Calcareous springs, high montane to alpine
cratoneurion.desc: Cold, lime-rich springs and seepages from the montane to the alpine belt. Tufa mosses, butterworts and yellow mountain saxifrage grow in the trickling water. Small in area but rich in specialists.
cratoneurion.sub: Sorgenti carbonatiche da altimontane ad alpine

montion.name: Springs on base-poor substrates
montion.desc: Springs and rivulets on base-poor rock (granite, gneiss, schist). Bright green mosses with starry saxifrage, blinks and bittercress. Water is cold and soft; typical of the central Alps.
montion.sub: Sorgenti dei substrati poveri di carbonati

phragmition.name: Reedbeds of still water
phragmition.desc: Tall reedbeds standing permanently in shallow, still water at lake and pond margins: common reed, bulrushes, club-rush and bur-reeds. Important for birds; strongly reduced in the valley floors.
phragmition.sub: Canneti ed altri consorzi elofitici di acque stagnanti con vegetazione regolarmente sommersa

phalaridion.name: Reedbeds of flowing water
phalaridion.desc: Reed and tall-grass stands along flowing water that are flooded only from time to time: reed canary-grass, sweet-grasses and watercress. Common along ditches and river banks.
phalaridion.sub: Canneti ed altri consorzi elofitici di acque più o meno ruscellanti con vegetazione solo periodicamente sommersa

littorelletea.name: Amphibious shore and ephemeral pool vegetation
littorelletea.desc: Short, amphibious vegetation on the exposed mud of lake shores and temporary pools, often of small annuals that appear only in dry summers. Many species are critically endangered because such shores have almost disappeared.
littorelletea.sub: Vegetazione anfibia delle sponde di laghi e stagni nonché di pozze temporanee

molinion.name: Nutrient-poor wet meadows with purple moor-grass
molinion.desc: Late-mown, unfertilised wet meadows on peaty or clayey soils dominated by purple moor-grass. Rich in rare flowers such as marsh gentian and Siberian iris. Depends on one late cut a year; lost through drainage, fertilising or abandonment.
molinion.sub: Praterie umide magre (povere di nutrienti) a Molinia caerulea

calthion.name: Nutrient-rich wet meadows with marsh marigold
calthion.desc: Fertilised wet meadows on nutrient-rich, waterlogged soils, colourful in spring with marsh marigold and in summer with cabbage thistle and bistort. Found in valley bottoms and on spring-fed slopes.
calthion.sub: Praterie umide ricche di nutrienti a Caltha palustris

cladietum.name: Great fen-sedge beds
cladietum.desc: Dense stands of great fen-sedge in calcareous, spring-fed fens of the valley floor. Very rare in South Tyrol and a priority habitat in the EU.

magnocaricion.name: Tall-sedge swamps
magnocaricion.desc: Swamps dominated by large sedges that form tussocks or dense stands, usually at the landward edge of reedbeds or in silted hollows. They stay flooded for much of the year.

caricionfuscae.name: Acidic small-sedge fens
caricionfuscae.desc: Low, acidic fens with small sedges, cottongrasses and peat mosses, fed by base-poor water. Widespread in the siliceous central Alps from the montane to the alpine belt.
caricionfuscae.sub: Vegetazione torbicola o palustre, acidofila, a carici di taglia ridotta

davallianae.name: Calcareous small-sedge fens
davallianae.desc: Low fens fed by calcareous spring water, with Davall's sedge, bird's-eye primrose, orchids and broad-leaved cottongrass. Among the richest and most threatened habitats in the Alps.
davallianae.sub: Vegetazione torbicola neutro-basifila, a carici di taglia ridotta

transition.name: Transition mires and quaking bogs
transition.desc: Quaking mires between fen and bog: a floating, wet mat of sedges, bogbean and peat mosses. Home to sundews and several glacial relict sedges. Extremely sensitive to drainage and trampling.

raisedbog.name: Raised bogs with peat mosses
raisedbog.desc: Peat bodies built by peat mosses that have grown above the groundwater and are fed only by rain. Hummocks and hollows with cottongrass, bog rosemary and cranberries. A priority habitat; peat grows less than 1 mm a year.

atrofusco.name: Pioneer vegetation of glacial-stream alluvium
atrofusco.desc: Open pioneer vegetation on fine, cold alluvium of glacier-fed streams in the alpine belt. Small sedges and rushes of arctic origin. A priority habitat, threatened by glacier retreat and hydropower.
atrofusco.sub: Vegetazione pioniera delle alluvioni dei torrenti glaciali

epilobion.name: Herbaceous pioneers on torrent gravel bars
epilobion.desc: First colonisers of fresh gravel bars along mountain rivers: alpine willowherb, butterburs and gypsophila. They depend on floods that keep creating new bare gravel.
epilobion.sub: Vegetazione erbacea pioniera delle alluvioni dei greti torrentizi

salicion.name: Riverside willow scrub on gravel
salicion.desc: Willow scrub on gravel bars and banks of rivers that flood regularly: olive, purple and violet willows, sea buckthorn and German tamarisk. Typical of natural river corridors like the upper Ahr and Etsch.
salicion.sub: Arbusteti ripariali e torrentizi a salici di ripa

potentilletalia.name: Calcareous rock faces
potentilletalia.desc: Plants rooted in crevices of limestone and dolomite cliffs. Many are endemics of the southern Alps, such as devil's claw and Moretti's bellflower. Cliffs of the Dolomites are a hotspot.

androsacetalia.name: Siliceous rock faces
androsacetalia.desc: Crevice vegetation on granite, gneiss, porphyry and schist cliffs. Hairy primrose, forked spleenwort and furrowed saxifrage are typical.

thlaspietalia.name: Calcareous and base-rich scree
thlaspietalia.syn: Thlaspietalia rotundifolii, Drabetalia hoppeanae, Stipion calamagrostis
thlaspietalia.desc: Plants of moving limestone, dolomite and calcschist scree. They anchor themselves with long roots and runners. Four sub-units: fine alpine scree (Thlaspion), coarse moist scree (Petasition), high-alpine calcschist (Drabion) and warm low-altitude scree (Stipion).

units.label: Stipion - warm, dry scree at low altitude

thlaspietalia.sub: Vegetazione dei detriti di falda a matrice carbonatica o non povera di basi

androsacetaliaalpinae.name: Siliceous scree
androsacetaliaalpinae.desc: Plants of siliceous scree and moraines, from the montane belt up to the summits. In the alpine belt glacier buttercup and glacier rock-jasmine; lower down, hemp-nettles on stony slopes.

units.label: Androsacion and Allosuro-Athyrion - alpine silicate scree

androsacetaliaalpinae.sub: Vegetazione dei detriti di falda a matrice silicatica e suoli calciocarenti

alyssosedion.name: Open vegetation on calcareous or base-rich rock outcrops
alyssosedion.desc: Thin, open vegetation of succulents, annuals and mosses on bare limestone or base-rich rock where the soil is only a few centimetres deep. A priority habitat in the warm valleys.
alyssosedion.sub: Vegetazione discontinua di ambienti rupestri primitivi a matrice carbonatica o anche silicatica ma non povera di basi

sedoscleranthetalia.name: Open vegetation on dry acidic or serpentine rock outcrops
sedoscleranthetalia.desc: Open vegetation of houseleeks, stonecrops and tiny annuals on dry siliceous or serpentine rock outcrops. Very rich in rare annual grasses at low altitude.
sedoscleranthetalia.sub: Vegetazione discontinua di ambienti arido-rupestri primitivi a matrice silicatica acida o serpentinitica

seslerietalia.name: Calcareous alpine grasslands
seslerietalia.desc: Natural grasslands on limestone and dolomite above the treeline. Four types: blue moor-grass slopes, cushion sedge on wind-swept ridges, rusty sedge on deep moist soils, and Elyna ridges. Home of edelweiss and many gentians.

units.label: Caricion firmae - wind-blown cushion sedge swards
Caricion ferrugineae - rusty sedge swards on moist, deep soils

caricetea.name: Acidic primary alpine grasslands
caricetea.desc: Natural grasslands on acidic rock above the treeline. Curved sedge dominates above 2,300 m; variegated fescue on steep sunny slopes; mat-grass where soils are deeper. Covers large areas of the central Alps.

arabidion.name: Calcareous snowbeds
arabidion.desc: Hollows on limestone and calcschist where snow lies until July, leaving only 2-3 months of growing season. Dwarf willows, Bavarian gentian and blue rock-cress.

salicionherbaceae.name: Acidic snowbeds
salicionherbaceae.desc: Hollows on acidic rock where snow lies longest. Dominated by dwarf willow, a tree reduced to a couple of leaves, with snowbell and dwarf cudweed.

calamagrostion.name: Tall-grass swards on calcareous slopes
calamagrostion.desc: Tall, unmown grass stands of variegated small-reed on steep, moist limestone slopes in the montane and subalpine belts.
calamagrostion.sub: Praterie montane incolte ad alte erbe dei suoli basifili

calamagrostietalia.name: Montane-subalpine tall herbs on silicate
calamagrostietalia.desc: Tall grasses and herbs on siliceous soils, often in avalanche tracks, clearings and along forest edges in the subalpine belt.
calamagrostietalia.sub: Comunità ad alte erbe montano-subalpine su silicati

mesobromion.name: Semi-dry grasslands
mesobromion.desc: Species-rich, unfertilised grasslands on moderately dry soils, traditionally mown once a year. Upright brome and many orchids. One of the richest habitats in Europe; lost to fertilisation or abandonment.
mesobromion.sub: Praterie semiaride da subatlantiche a subcontinentali

stipion.name: Continental steppe grasslands
stipion.desc: Steppe-like grasslands on the hottest, driest slopes of the inner valleys (Vinschgau, Eisack and Etsch valleys). Feather-grasses and continental species far from their main range. A priority habitat.

xerobromion.name: Hot, dry sub-Mediterranean grasslands
xerobromion.desc: Very dry, open grasslands on shallow, sunny soils of the warmest southern valleys, with sub-Mediterranean grasses.

nardetalia.name: Mat-grass pastures and acid grasslands
nardetalia.desc: Grazed, nutrient-poor grasslands on acidic soils, dominated by wiry mat-grass. Rich in arnica, gentians and orchids. A priority habitat when species-rich.
nardetalia.sub: Prati e pascoli magri e acidi con nardo e comunità affini

poion.name: Rich montane-subalpine pastures
poion.desc: Rich pastures around alpine huts and resting places, fertilised by grazing animals. Alpine meadow-grass and brown clover are excellent fodder.

arrhenatherion.name: Lowland hay meadows
arrhenatherion.desc: Fertilised hay meadows of the valleys and lower slopes, mown two or three times a year, with false oat-grass and colourful flowers. Species-rich only when manured moderately.
arrhenatherion.sub: Prati pingui dal fondovalle alla fascia bassomontana

trisetion.name: Mountain hay meadows
trisetion.desc: Fertilised hay meadows of the mountains, mown once or twice a year, colourful with wood crane's-bill, bistort and globeflower. A classic South Tyrolean landscape.

brachypodium.name: Abandoned grasslands with tor-grass or tall purple moor-grass
brachypodium.desc: Former meadows and pastures that are no longer mown or grazed, now overgrown by tor-grass or tall purple moor-grass. A transitional stage towards scrub and forest.
brachypodium.sub: Praterie incolte, da submontane ad altimontane, a dominanza di Brachypodium spp. e/o di Molinia arundinacea

trifoliogeranietea.name: Warm forest fringes and grassy glades
trifoliogeranietea.desc: Herb-rich fringes between forest and grassland on warm, dry slopes, with bloody crane's-bill, burning bush and many legumes. Sub-units for dry, mesic and acidic fringes.

calystegietalia.name: Damp riverside fringes
calystegietalia.desc: Tall, nutrient-rich herb fringes along rivers and streams, with bindweed, nettles and comfrey. Often invaded by alien species such as Himalayan balsam and goldenrods.

units.label: Petasition (differential species) - butterbur stands along mountain streams

hackelion.name: Rock overhangs used as shelter by ungulates
hackelion.desc: Dry, nitrogen-rich ground under overhanging rocks where chamois, ibex and sheep shelter. A specialised flora of nitrophilous annuals.

epilobietea.name: Woodland clearings
epilobietea.desc: Tall herbs that colonise clearings after felling, windthrow or fire: rosebay willowherb, raspberry and foxgloves. A short-lived stage before shrubs and trees return.

filipendulenion.name: Wet tall-herb stands
filipendulenion.desc: Tall, wet herb stands with meadowsweet along ditches, streams and abandoned wet meadows.

adenostylion.name: Subalpine tall-herb stands
adenostylion.desc: Lush, tall herb stands on moist, nutrient-rich soils in the subalpine belt, often below green alder or along streams. Alpine butterbur, monkshood and alpine blue-sow-thistle.

prunetalia.name: Hedges, thickets and forest mantles
prunetalia.desc: Hedges, thickets and the shrubby mantle along forest edges. Important for birds and insects. Sub-units for warm and dry, mesic, and pioneer thickets.

salicioncinereae.name: Grey willow swamp scrub
salicioncinereae.desc: Wet willow scrub of grey willow at the margins of fens and in silted hollows.

subalpinewillow.name: Subalpine willow scrub
subalpinewillow.desc: Scrub of various shrubby willows on moist, long-snow slopes and along streams in the subalpine belt.

mughete.name: Mountain pine scrub
mughete.syn: Erico-Pinion mugo p.p., Rhododendro ferruginei-Pinetum prostratae
mughete.desc: Dense, creeping thickets of mountain pine on limestone scree and avalanche tracks, and on acidic rock with alpenrose. A priority habitat under the EU Habitats Directive.
mughete.sub: Mughete di substrati carbonatici o silicatici

mughetetorbiera.name: Mountain pine on raised bogs
mughetetorbiera.desc: Mountain pine growing on raised bogs, with peat mosses, cottongrass and bog berries in the understorey.

alnetumviridis.name: Green alder scrub
alnetumviridis.desc: Dense green alder scrub on moist, avalanche-swept north slopes, with lush tall herbs in the understorey.
alnetumviridis.sub: Arbusteti subalpini subigrofili a ontano verde

ericion.name: Calcareous dwarf-shrub heath
ericion.desc: Low heath of winter heath, hairy alpenrose and bearberries on limestone and dolomite in the montane and subalpine belts.

rhodovaccinion.name: Alpenrose heath on acidic soils
rhodovaccinion.desc: Heath of alpenrose, bilberry and cowberry on acidic soils at and above the treeline, where snow protects the shrubs in winter.

loiseleurio.name: Wind-swept dwarf azalea heath
loiseleurio.desc: Low, wind-swept heath of trailing azalea, crowberry and lichens on acidic ridges where snow is blown away.
loiseleurio.sub: Brughiera bassa acidofila ad azalea nana e mirtillo

juniperion.name: Dry dwarf-juniper heath and warm savin juniper scrub
juniperion.desc: Dry heath of dwarf juniper on sunny siliceous slopes in the subalpine belt; at lower altitude in the inner valleys, warm scrub with savin juniper.
juniperion.sub: Landa subalpina xerofila a ginepro nano e termofila a ginepro sabino, con ericacee

cembrete.name: Swiss stone pine and larch-stone pine forests
cembrete.desc: Forests of Swiss stone pine, often mixed with larch, at the treeline on acidic soils. Alpenrose and bilberry form the understorey.

lariceti.name: Larch forests
lariceti.desc: Open larch forests, often managed as wooded pastures. Larch lets light through, so the understorey is rich in grasses and dwarf shrubs.

pecceteSub.name: Subalpine spruce forests
pecceteSub.desc: Spruce forests of the subalpine belt and on extreme sites such as block screes, where other trees cannot compete.

pecceteMont.name: Montane spruce forests
pecceteMont.desc: Spruce-dominated forests of the montane belt, the most common forest type in South Tyrol.

piceoabieteti.name: Spruce-fir forests
piceoabieteti.desc: Mixed forests of spruce and silver fir on moist, deep soils of the montane belt.

piceoabietifaggeti.name: Spruce-fir-beech forests
piceoabietifaggeti.desc: Mixed mountain forests of spruce, silver fir and beech, mainly in the south and east of the province.

faggete.name: Beech forests
faggete.desc: Beech forests, mostly in the south of the province (Unterland, Überetsch) and on moist slopes of the montane belt. Sub-units for rich, south-eastern Alpine and acidic beech forests.

pinete.name: Montane Scots pine forests
pinete.desc: Scots pine forests on dry, poor soils. Sub-units for acidic pine woods, steppe pine woods of the inner valleys, and heath pine woods on limestone.

units.label: Ononido-Pinion and Deschampsio-Pinion - steppe pine forests of the inner valleys
Erico-Pinetalia - heath pine forests on limestone

bagolaro.name: Warm siliceous block screes with nettle tree
bagolaro.desc: Warm block screes and rocky slopes on porphyry or granite at low altitude, colonised by nettle tree, sweet chestnut and hop-hornbeam.

quercopinete.name: Oak-pine forests
quercopinete.desc: Mixed forests of sessile or downy oak and Scots pine on warm, dry slopes.

querceti.name: Oak forests
querceti.desc: Oak forests of downy and sessile oak on warm slopes of the lower valleys.

ornoostrieti.name: Manna ash and hop-hornbeam woods
ornoostrieti.desc: Woods of manna ash and hop-hornbeam on warm, dry, mostly calcareous or porphyry slopes in the south.

frassinotiglieti.name: Ash-lime and maple ravine forests
frassinotiglieti.desc: Mixed forests of ash, lime, maple and elm on rocky, moist slopes, in ravines and at the foot of cliffs.

betulion.name: Bog woodland
betulion.desc: Woodlands of birch, spruce and pine growing on peat at the edge of bogs.

alnetaincana.name: Grey alder woods
alnetaincana.desc: Grey alder woods along mountain rivers, flooded from time to time.

grete.name: Riverside willow and pine woods on gravel
grete.desc: Riverside woods and scrub of willows and pine on gravel bars and banks.
grete.sub: Saliceti e pinete di greto e/o ripariali

alnofrassineti.name: Alder-ash floodplain forests
alnofrassineti.desc: Floodplain forests of alder and ash along slow rivers on wet, nutrient-rich soils.

Chara sp..d: Green algae resembling small horsetails, with whorled branches and often a crust of lime. Form underwater meadows in clear lakes.

Nitella sp..d: Delicate stonewort algae with forked branchlets and no lime crust. Form underwater meadows in clear lakes.

Sphagnum sp..d: Mosses that soak up water like a sponge and slowly build peat; their tips stay green or red while the lower parts die and accumulate. The engineers of bogs and mires.

Utricularia bremii.d: Small bladderwort with delicate, divided leaves and pale yellow flowers. Critically endangered in shallow bog pools.

Utricularia minor.d: Small bladderwort with pale yellow flowers and leaves with few bladders. Grows in bog pools and fen hollows.

Elodea canadensis.d: Submerged plant with dense whorls of three small, dark green leaves along brittle stems. Introduced from North America; spreads quickly in lakes, ponds and slow ditches.

Groenlandia densa.d: Submerged pondweed with short, opposite, densely crowded leaves that clasp the stem; small green flower heads on short stalks. Grows in clear, cold, spring-fed water; endangered.

Myriophyllum spicatum.d: Submerged plant with whorls of feathery leaves and pinkish flower spikes raised above the water. Grows in lakes and slow rivers.

Najas marina.d: Submerged annual with stiff, brittle stems and narrow leaves with spiny teeth. Grows in warm, shallow lakes.

Potamogeton alpinus.d: Pondweed with reddish submerged leaves and floating, slightly leathery leaves. Grows in cold, clear lakes and slow streams.

Potamogeton crispus.d: Pondweed with four-angled stems and narrow, strongly wavy-edged, finely toothed leaves. Grows in ponds and ditches.

Potamogeton lucens.d: Fully submerged pondweed with large, glossy, translucent, oblong leaves with wavy edges and a short point. Grows in calcareous lakes; endangered.

Potamogeton pectinatus.d: Pondweed with thread-like, branching leaves forming dense underwater tufts. Grows in lakes and slow rivers.

Potamogeton pusillus agg..d: Slender, submerged pondweed with narrow, grass-like leaves and tiny flower spikes. Grows in ponds, ditches and lake margins.

Ranunculus trichophyllus.d: Aquatic buttercup with thread-like submerged leaves and small white flowers just above the water. Grows in ponds, ditches and slow streams.

Nuphar lutea.d: Floating, heart-shaped leaves and cup-shaped yellow flowers raised above the water. Grows in lakes and ponds.

Nymphaea alba.d: Large, round floating leaves with a deep slit and big, many-petalled white flowers with a yellow centre, opening in sunshine. Grows in the few natural lakes and ponds of the lowlands; protected.

Potamogeton natans.d: Pondweed with oval, leathery floating leaves on long stalks that bend at the base of the blade. Grows in ponds and lakes.

Lemna minor.d: Tiny floating plant with oval, lens-shaped fronds about 3 mm long, each with a single root. Covers ponds and ditches with a green film.

Spirodela polyrhiza.d: Floating plant with round fronds up to 1 cm, purple beneath, each with a bundle of roots. Grows on still ponds; critically endangered.

Utricularia australis.d: Free-floating carnivorous plant with finely divided leaves bearing tiny bladders that suck in prey; yellow flowers above water. Grows in ponds.

Berula erecta.d: Aquatic umbellifer with pinnate leaves, toothed leaflets and small white umbels opposite the leaves. Grows in clear, slow-flowing spring-fed streams and ditches.

Nasturtium officinale agg..d: Aquatic plant with glossy, pinnate leaves and small white flowers. Grows in clear, cool spring-fed water.

Sparganium emersum.d: Plant with long, keeled leaves and an unbranched spike of spherical flower heads. Grows in ponds and slow streams.

Dermatocarpon rivulorum.d: Leafy, brownish lichen attached at one point to rocks in cold, clear mountain streams; it turns green and soft when wet. An indicator of clean, fast-flowing water.

Fontinalis antipyretica.d: Large aquatic moss with dark green, three-ranked, keeled leaves, trailing in long streamers in the current. Grows in mountain streams, springs and clear lakes.

Scapania undulata.d: Leafy liverwort with wavy, two-lobed leaves, often reddish. Grows on rocks in acidic mountain streams.

Adiantum capillus-veneris.d: Delicate fern with shiny black stalks and fan-shaped, wedge-like leaflets. Restricted to dripping, sheltered limestone walls and tufa springs in the warmest valleys.

Arabis soyeri subsp. subcoriacea.d: Glossy, almost leathery-leaved rock-cress with white flowers. Grows in cold, calcareous springs and wet seepages of the high mountains.

Cratoneuron spp..d: Robust mosses of calcareous springs whose feathery shoots get coated with lime; over time the deposits build porous tufa rock. The key organisms of petrifying springs.

Epilobium alsinifolium.d: Small willowherb with glossy, bluish-green, chickweed-like leaves and pinkish-violet flowers; spreads with fleshy runners. Grows in cold mountain springs and along alpine rivulets.

Pinguicula alpina.d: Carnivorous plant with a rosette of pale, sticky leaves that trap small insects and white flowers with yellow spots on the lip. Grows in calcareous springs and fens.

Pinguicula vulgaris.d: Carnivorous plant with a star-shaped rosette of yellow-green, sticky, greasy leaves and violet, spurred flowers. Grows in springs, fens and wet rocks.

Saxifraga aizoides.d: Mat-forming saxifrage with fleshy, narrow leaves and yellow to orange flowers. Grows along streams, springs and damp scree.

Carex frigida.d: Loosely tufted sedge with glossy leaves and drooping, blackish-brown female spikes on long stalks. Grows beside icy springs, rivulets and seepages from the montane belt up to the alpine zone.

Epilobium nutans.d: Small willowherb whose flower bud nods before opening; small pink flowers. Grows in cold springs and acidic fens.

Montia fontana.d: Tiny, succulent plant with opposite, spoon-shaped leaves and inconspicuous white flowers. Grows in cold springs and rivulets on acidic rock.

Saxifraga stellaris.d: Saxifrage with a rosette of toothed leaves and star-shaped white flowers with two yellow spots on each petal. Grows in cold springs and along rivulets.

Sedum villosum.d: Small, glandular-hairy stonecrop with fleshy leaves and pale pink flowers. Critically endangered in cold, acidic springs.

Equisetum fluviatile.d: Horsetail with smooth, hollow stems, usually unbranched or with few whorls. Stands in shallow water at lake and pond edges.

Glyceria maxima.d: Tall grass, up to 2 m, forming dense stands with large, branched panicles. Grows at lake and river edges.

Phragmites australis.d: Tall grass up to 3 m with stiff stems, broad grey-green leaves and large, silky, purple-brown panicles. Forms dense reedbeds at lake shores and in wet hollows.

Schoenoplectus lacustris.d: Tall, rush-like plant with round, leafless green stems up to 3 m and brown flower clusters near the top. Grows in lakes and ponds.

Sparganium erectum.d: Reedbed plant with stiff, keeled leaves and a branched spike of spherical heads. Grows in reedbeds and ditches.

Typha angustifolia.d: Bulrush with narrow leaves; the male and female parts of the brown spike are separated by a gap. Grows in reedbeds; endangered.

Typha latifolia.d: Tall plant with broad, flat leaves and a thick, dark brown, sausage-like spike. Grows in reedbeds at pond margins.

Calamagrostis canescens.d: Slender reed-like grass with grey-green leaves and soft, purplish panicles. Formerly in tall-sedge fens and willow carr; listed as regionally extinct.

Glyceria fluitans.d: Grass whose leaves often float on the water; long, narrow panicles with long spikelets. Grows in ditches, springs and slow streams.

Glyceria notata.d: Sweet-grass with folded young leaves and short, few-flowered spikelets on spreading branches. Grows in ditches, springs and muddy, slow-flowing water.

Leersia oryzoides.d: Grass with very rough, cutting leaf edges and a panicle that often stays hidden in the upper leaf sheath. Rare along ditches and muddy pond margins.

Phalaris arundinacea.d: Tall grass up to 2 m with broad leaves and dense, lobed, purplish panicles. Forms stands along rivers, ditches and lake margins.

Cyperus flavescens.d: Small, tufted annual sedge with flat clusters of yellowish spikelets surrounded by leafy bracts. Grows on damp mud of drying pond margins in summer.

Cyperus fuscus.d: Small annual sedge with dense clusters of very dark brown spikelets and long leafy bracts. Grows on exposed mud of pond edges and temporarily flooded hollows.

Gnaphalium uliginosum.d: Small, branched, woolly annual with tiny brownish heads surrounded by leafy bracts. Grows on damp mud at pond margins and in wheel ruts.

Juncus bufonius.d: Small, branched annual rush, 3-25 cm, with thread-like leaves and pale green flowers scattered along the branches. Grows on damp mud of pond margins and in wheel ruts.

Limosella aquatica.d: Tiny annual with long-stalked, spoon-shaped leaves in a rosette and minute white or pink flowers. Very rare on wet mud of drying ponds.

Peplis portula.d: Tiny creeping annual with opposite, spoon-shaped leaves and minute reddish flowers in the leaf axils. Critically endangered on wet mud of pond margins.

Ranunculus flammula.d: Buttercup with narrow, spear-shaped, untoothed leaves and small, glossy yellow flowers. Grows on wet mud at pond margins; endangered.

Rorippa islandica.d: Small crucifer with deeply lobed leaves, tiny yellow flowers and plump pods. Grows on damp mud of pond margins and riverbanks.

Carex tomentosa.d: Sedge with a creeping rhizome, bluish leaves and short, round female spikes whose fruits are densely covered in fine white hairs. Grows in nutrient-poor wet meadows with purple moor-grass.

Festuca trichophylla.d: Fescue spreading with slender runners, with hair-fine, rolled leaves and loose reddish panicles. A rare grass of nutrient-poor wet meadows with purple moor-grass.

Gentiana asclepiadea.d: Tall gentian with paired, willow-like leaves and rows of deep blue flowers in late summer. Grows in moist meadows and woods.

Gentiana pneumonanthe.d: Gentian with narrow leaves and deep blue trumpet flowers striped green outside, opening in late summer. Very rare in nutrient-poor wet meadows; critically endangered.

Iris sibirica.d: Iris with narrow, grass-like leaves and blue-violet flowers with darker veins on hollow stems taller than the leaves. Critically endangered in the last nutrient-poor wet meadows.

Juncus conglomeratus.d: Tufted rush with ridged, dull stems and a dense, ball-like cluster of brown flowers. Grows in wet, acidic meadows and pastures.

Juncus effusus.d: Tall rush with smooth, glossy stems filled with white pith and a loose, spreading flower cluster near the top. Common in wet meadows and pastures.

Laserpitium prutenicum.d: Hairy umbellifer with twice-pinnate leaves and white umbels; fruits with four wavy wings. Rare in nutrient-poor wet meadows with purple moor-grass.

Lathyrus palustris.d: Climbing pea with winged stems, narrow leaflets, tendrils and pale violet-blue flowers. Very rare in wet meadows and fens.

Lotus maritimus.d: Creeping legume with bluish trifoliate leaves and large, single, pale yellow flowers; four-winged pods. Grows in nutrient-poor wet meadows.

Molinia caerulea.d: Tussock grass with dark purple panicles and stems without nodes along most of their length. Leading grass of nutrient-poor wet meadows and bogs.

Ophioglossum vulgatum.d: Small fern with a single oval leaf and a fertile spike. Rare in wet meadows.

Scorzonera humilis.d: Plant with narrow, grass-like leaves and single pale yellow heads with woolly bracts. Grows in nutrient-poor wet meadows.

Selinum carvifolia.d: Umbellifer with sharply angled stems, finely divided leaves and white umbels. Grows in nutrient-poor wet meadows.

Serratula tinctoria.d: Slender plant with finely toothed, often pinnate leaves and narrow purple flower heads. Grows in nutrient-poor wet meadows.

Succisa pratensis.d: Plant with untoothed leaves and round, blue-violet flower heads in late summer; the root looks bitten off. Grows in nutrient-poor wet meadows.

Caltha palustris.d: Glossy, kidney-shaped leaves and large, cup-shaped, golden-yellow flowers in spring. Typical of wet meadows, springs and stream edges.

Cirsium oleraceum.d: Tall, soft-spined thistle with pale green, clasping leaves and clusters of pale yellow flower heads surrounded by large, yellowish bracts. Abundant in wet meadows and along ditches.

Crepis paludosa.d: Hawk's-beard with clasping, toothed stem leaves and orange-yellow heads whose bracts are covered in black glandular hairs. Grows in wet meadows, springs and along streams.

Equisetum palustre.d: Horsetail with deeply furrowed stems, black-tipped sheaths and regular whorls of branches. Grows in wet meadows; poisonous to livestock.

Filipendula ulmaria.d: Tall perennial with pinnate leaves silvery beneath and frothy, fragrant cream flowers. Grows in wet tall-herb stands and ditches.

Juncus filiformis.d: Rush with very thin stems; the bract above the small flower cluster is as long as the stem itself. Grows in fens, wet meadows and lake shores in the mountains.

Lotus pedunculatus.d: Taller relative of bird's-foot trefoil with hollow stems and heads of 5-12 yellow flowers. Very rare in wet meadows.

Persicaria bistorta.d: Perennial with long, oval leaves on winged stalks and dense, cylindrical spikes of pink flowers. Abundant in mountain hay meadows and wet meadows.

Scirpus sylvaticus.d: Club-rush with broad, grass-like leaves and large, branched clusters of small greenish-brown spikelets. Grows in wet meadows and along ditches.

Trollius europaeus.d: Plant with palmately divided leaves and spherical, lemon-yellow flowers that never open fully. Grows in mountain hay meadows and wet pastures.

Cladium mariscus.d: Robust, evergreen sedge up to 2 m with long, saw-edged leaves that cut skin and branched clusters of brown spikelets. Forms dense stands in calcareous fens; very rare in South Tyrol.

Peucedanum palustre.d: Umbellifer with hollow, furrowed stems, white milky sap and white umbels with bent-back bracts. Grows in tall-sedge fens and willow carr; endangered.

Scutellaria galericulata.d: Plant with four-angled stems, toothed leaves and pairs of blue-violet, hooded flowers in the leaf axils. Grows in tall-sedge fens and willow carr.

Carex acuta.d: Tall sedge with sharply three-angled stems, drooping female spikes and several male spikes. Forms stands in tall-sedge swamps and ditches.

Carex acutiformis.d: Robust sedge spreading with rhizomes, with broad bluish leaves and several dark male spikes. Very common in tall-sedge swamps and wet ditches.

Carex appropinquata.d: Forms tall tussocks whose base is wrapped in black-brown, fibrous old sheaths; small brownish spikes in a loose, branched panicle. One of the rarest sedges of the valley-floor fens, surviving in a handful of tall-sedge swamps.

Carex disticha.d: Sedge with many spikes along a single stem; middle ones male. Very rare in tall-sedge fens in the valleys.

Carex elata.d: Sedge forming tall, firm tussocks with yellowish leaves and several narrow spikes. Dominant in tall-sedge swamps around lakes.

Carex otrubae.d: Robust sedge with a dense, branched head of greenish-brown spikes. Grows in wet meadows, ditches and tall-sedge stands.

Carex paniculata.d: Builds massive tussocks up to 1 m tall with sharply three-angled stems and a large, branched panicle of brown spikes. Grows in tall-sedge fens and spring-fed swamps.

Carex pseudocyperus.d: Bright green sedge with long, cylindrical, drooping female spikes on slender stalks, densely set with spreading, beaked fruits. Grows at the margins of ponds and in tall-sedge stands in the valley floors.

Carex riparia.d: Very large sedge, up to 1.5 m, with broad, bluish leaves and stout female spikes; several dark brown male spikes on top. Forms stands in tall-sedge swamps and along ditches at low altitude.

Carex rostrata.d: Sedge with bluish leaves and cylindrical spikes of inflated, beaked fruits. Common in fens, mires and tall-sedge swamps.

Carex vesicaria.d: Tall, yellow-green sedge with sharply three-angled stems and long, cylindrical spikes of inflated, beaked fruits. Grows in tall-sedge swamps, wet hollows and lake margins.

Senecio paludosus.d: Tall ragwort, 1-2 m, with long, narrow, saw-toothed leaves woolly beneath and golden-yellow heads. Critically endangered in tall-sedge swamps of the valley floors.

Agrostis canina.d: Fine-leaved creeping grass with delicate reddish panicles that close after flowering. Typical of acidic small-sedge fens and wet, nutrient-poor peat.

Carex canescens.d: Tufted sedge with grey-green leaves and short, pale spikes spaced along the stem. Typical of acidic fens and bog woodland.

Carex echinata.d: Small tufted sedge whose 3-4 rounded spikes carry fruits spreading outwards like tiny stars. Common in acidic fens, spring mires and wet peaty pastures from the valleys to the subalpine belt.

Carex nigra.d: Loosely tufted sedge with stiff, grey-green leaves and 2-4 narrow, black-brown female spikes below one or two male spikes. The commonest sedge of acidic fens, wet meadows and spring mires.

Carex paupercula.d: Slender sedge with bluish leaves and dark, nodding female spikes on thin stalks; the bracts are long and leafy. Grows in acidic fens, bog margins and sphagnum lawns in the subalpine belt.

Comarum palustre.d: Creeping perennial with grey-green, five- to seven-lobed leaves and star-shaped, deep wine-red flowers. Grows in transition mires, fens and at the edges of bog pools.

Eriophorum angustifolium.d: Spreads with rhizomes; narrow, channelled leaves and several nodding white cotton heads per stem on smooth stalks. Common in acidic fens, bogs and wet pastures.

Eriophorum scheuchzeri.d: Cottongrass with a single, round, snow-white head per stem. Grows at the edges of alpine pools and fens.

Salix repens subsp. rosmarinifolia.it: Salice strisciante a foglie di rosmarino

Trichophorum caespitosum.d: Dense tufts of thin, round, bright green stems each topped by a single small brown spikelet. Common in acidic fens, bogs and wet heaths.

Viola palustris.d: Small violet with kidney-shaped leaves and pale lilac flowers with dark veins. Grows in acidic fens and bogs.

Carex davalliana.d: Dense tufted sedge with single small spikes; male and female plants separate. Leading species of calcareous small-sedge fens.

Carex dioica.d: Small sedge spreading with thin runners; each stem carries a single spike, male and female on separate plants. Grows in calcareous small-sedge fens.

Carex panicea.d: Sedge with bluish leaves similar to carnation leaves and plump, olive fruits. Typical of calcareous fens and wet meadows.

Dactylorhiza incarnata subsp. cruenta.d: Marsh orchid with leaves spotted dark purple on both sides and a dense spike of purple flowers. Very rare in calcareous fens.

Eriophorum latifolium.d: Tufted cottongrass with flat leaves and several drooping heads on rough stalks; no runners. A typical plant of calcareous fens and spring mires.

Gentiana utriculosa.d: Annual gentian with a strongly winged, inflated calyx and deep blue star flowers. Grows in calcareous fens and wet meadows.

Liparis loeselii.d: Small, yellow-green orchid with two shiny, keeled leaves and a few inconspicuous flowers. Critically endangered in the last calcareous fens.

Primula farinosa.d: Small primrose with leaves white-mealy beneath and umbels of pink flowers with a yellow eye. Grows in calcareous fens and wet meadows.

Schoenus ferrugineus.d: Tufted sedge with a small, dark red-brown head and a short bract. Grows in calcareous small-sedge fens.

Schoenus nigricans.d: Tufted sedge with a compact head of shiny black spikelets and a longer bract. Grows in calcareous fens.

Spiranthes aestivalis.d: Slender orchid with narrow leaves and a spiral spike of small, white, fragrant flowers. Formerly in calcareous fens; regionally extinct.

Swertia perennis.d: Perennial with a spike of star-shaped, steel-blue to violet flowers with dark veins. Grows in calcareous fens and spring mires.

Typha minima.d: Small bulrush, 30-80 cm, with very thin leaves and a short, round to oval brown spike. A pioneer of fresh sand along wild rivers; regionally extinct in South Tyrol.

Carex chordorrhiza.d: Sedge with long, creeping stems lying on the moss and short, compact heads. A great rarity of transition mires.

Carex diandra.d: Slender sedge with a compact, dark brown, cylindrical head of small spikes and glossy, dark fruits. Grows in transition mires and quaking fens.

Carex heleonastes.d: Slender, grey-green sedge with three or four small, pale brown spikes clustered at the top of a rough stem. A glacial relict known from very few transition mires in South Tyrol.

Carex lasiocarpa.d: Sedge with long, very narrow, grey-green leaves rolled almost like a rush and densely hairy fruits. Spreads with rhizomes through the wettest parts of transition mires and quaking fens.

Carex limosa.d: Bluish-grey sedge with a creeping rhizome; female spikes hang on slender stalks below a single upright male spike. Grows in wet, muddy hollows of transition mires.

Drosera anglica.d: Carnivorous plant with long, upright, narrow leaves covered with red, sticky, glandular hairs that trap insects. Grows in wet hollows of transition mires.

Drosera anglica × rotundifolia.d: Hybrid sundew with leaves intermediate between the two parents: obovate blades on long stalks. Grows in transition mires where both parents occur.

Drosera intermedia.d: Sundew with spoon-shaped leaves on long stalks and a flower stem that bends at the base. Very rare in transition mires.

Eriophorum gracile.d: Slender cottongrass with narrow, three-angled, channelled leaves and 2-5 small cotton heads on short, rough stalks. A boreal relict of the wettest hollows in transition mires; critically endangered.

Lycopodiella inundata.d: Small, creeping clubmoss with short, upright fertile shoots ending in a leafy cone. Colonises bare, wet peat in transition mires and is vulnerable in South Tyrol.

Menyanthes trifoliata.d: Aquatic plant with large trifoliate leaves and spikes of white, star-shaped flowers fringed with white hairs. Grows in transition mires and pools.

Rhynchospora alba.d: Slender, tufted sedge with compact heads of white spikelets that turn brownish with age. Grows in wet hollows of transition mires; vulnerable and protected.

Rhynchospora fusca.d: Small sedge spreading with creeping rhizomes, with dark brown spikelets overtopped by a long bract. Critically endangered in the wettest parts of transition mires.

Scheuchzeria palustris.d: Rush-like plant with sheathing leaves and inflated, green fruits. Grows in the wettest hollows of transition mires; endangered.

Trichophorum alpinum.d: Slender sedge with three-angled stems; after flowering each spikelet turns into a small tuft of white, cottony bristles. Grows in transition mires and fens.

Andromeda polifolia.d: Low evergreen shrub with narrow, leathery leaves rolled under at the margin, bluish beneath, and nodding pink urn-shaped flowers. A plant of raised bogs and bog woodland.

Calluna vulgaris.d: Small evergreen shrub with tiny scale-like leaves in four rows and spikes of pink-lilac flowers in late summer. Indicator of acidic, nutrient-poor soils.

Empetrum hermaphroditum.d: Evergreen, heather-like dwarf shrub with needle-like leaves rolled under at the edge and black berries. Grows in wind-exposed acidic heaths and on raised bogs.

Eriophorum vaginatum.d: Tussock-forming cottongrass with a single, upright cotton head per stem and an inflated upper leaf sheath. Characteristic of raised bogs.

Vaccinium microcarpum.d: Tiny, creeping evergreen shrub with very small, pointed leaves and small red berries. Grows on sphagnum hummocks of raised bogs.

Vaccinium myrtillus.d: Deciduous shrub with green, angled twigs, finely toothed leaves and blue-black berries. Covers the ground in acidic conifer woods and heaths.

Vaccinium oxycoccos.d: Creeping evergreen shrublet with thread-like stems, small leaves white beneath, pink flowers and red berries. Grows on raised bogs.

Vaccinium uliginosum.d: Deciduous shrub with brownish, round twigs, bluish-green untoothed leaves and blue berries with pale flesh. Grows in raised bogs, bog woodland and alpine heaths.

Vaccinium vitis-idaea.d: Evergreen shrublet with leathery, glossy leaves dotted with dark glands beneath, pinkish bell flowers and red berries. Grows in acidic conifer woods and heaths.

Carex bicolor.d: Small sedge with stalked, dark-and-pale spikes clustered at the stem top. A rare arctic-alpine plant of glacial-stream alluvium.

Carex microglochin.d: Tiny sedge with a single spike whose fruits bend down when ripe. A rare relict of glacial alluvium.

Juncus triglumis.d: Small rush, 5-15 cm, with a single head of three pale brown flowers. Grows on glacial alluvium and in alpine fens.

Kobresia simpliciuscula.d: Small sedge with a short, branched spike of dark brown spikelets. Grows on glacial alluvium and in calcareous alpine fens.

Calamagrostis epigejos.d: Robust, rhizomatous grass up to 1.5 m with stiff, rough leaves and dense, upright, purplish panicles. Forms large stands in clearings, on river gravels and disturbed ground.

Calamagrostis pseudophragmites.d: Grey-green, reed-like grass with nodding, purplish panicles. A pioneer of fresh sand and gravel bars along wild Alpine rivers.

Chlorocrepis staticifolia.d: Hawkweed with narrow, grass-like, bluish leaves and pale lemon-yellow flower heads on branched stems; spreads with underground runners. A pioneer of limestone scree and river gravels.

Chondrilla chondrilloides.d: Low, bushy plant with rush-like, almost leafless green stems and small yellow heads. A specialist of dynamic gravel bars along wild Alpine rivers; endangered by river regulation.

Epilobium fleischeri.d: Low willowherb with narrow leaves and large, open, purple-pink flowers. A pioneer of gravel bars along glacial and mountain rivers.

Erigeron acer subsp. angulosus.d: Fleabane with angled stems and small heads of pale purple ray florets around a yellow centre. A pioneer of river gravels.

Gypsophila repens.d: Creeping plant with narrow blue-green leaves and white or pink flowers. Grows on limestone scree and river gravels.

Petasites paradoxus.d: Butterbur with triangular, toothed leaves densely white-felted beneath and pale pink flower heads in early spring. Colonises moist limestone scree and river gravels.

Scrophularia juratensis.d: Figwort with finely divided, almost fern-like leaves and small dark red-brown flowers. Grows on limestone scree and river gravels.

Trifolium saxatile.d: Small, grey-hairy annual clover with tiny whitish heads hidden among the leaves. A rarity of river gravels in the Alps; endangered.

Hippophae rhamnoides.d: Thorny shrub with narrow, silvery-scaly leaves and bright orange berries. Grows on gravel bars along rivers and on dry slopes.

Myricaria germanica.d: Shrub with scale-like, bluish leaves and spikes of pink flowers. A pioneer of open gravel bars along wild rivers; endangered by river regulation.

Salix daphnoides.d: Tall shrub with violet, waxy-bloomed twigs and glossy leaves. A pioneer on gravel bars of mountain rivers.

Salix eleagnos.d: Shrub with very narrow leaves, white-felted beneath with rolled edges. Dominates riverside scrub on gravel.

Salix purpurea.d: Shrub with slender, purple twigs and narrow leaves broadest near the tip, often nearly opposite. Common on river gravels.

Androsace helvetica.d: Dense, hard, hemispherical cushion of grey-hairy rosettes studded with stalkless white flowers. Grows in crevices of limestone and dolomite cliffs at high altitude.

Asplenium ruta-muraria.d: Small fern with leathery, dull green fronds divided into wedge-shaped leaflets. Grows in crevices of limestone rocks and old mortared walls.

Asplenium viride.d: Small fern with green stalks (not black) and rows of rounded, toothed leaflets. Grows in shady crevices of limestone rocks and moist boulders.

Carex brachystachys.d: Delicate, tufted sedge with soft, thread-like leaves and slender, nodding female spikes on long hair-fine stalks. Hangs from moist, shady crevices and overhangs of limestone and dolomite cliffs.

Carex mucronata.d: Dense tufts of stiff, bristle-like, grey-green leaves; short stems carry a single small spike with pointed bracts. Grows in crevices and on ledges of limestone and dolomite cliffs.

Cystopteris alpina.d: Small fern with very finely divided, lacy fronds whose last segments are narrow and blunt. Grows in moist, shaded limestone crevices and among blocks in the alpine belt.

Cystopteris fragilis.d: Delicate fern with fragile stalks and twice-pinnate, soft fronds; round sori covered by a hood-like membrane. Common in rock crevices and on old walls.

Draba tomentosa.d: Small, grey cushion densely covered with star hairs, bearing small white flowers. Grows in crevices of limestone and dolomite cliffs.

Minuartia rupestris.d: Small, glandular-hairy cushion plant with white flowers. Grows in crevices of limestone and dolomite cliffs.

Moehringia muscosa.d: Delicate, moss-like plant with thread-like leaves and small white four-petalled flowers. Grows in shaded, moist limestone crevices.

Potentilla caulescens.d: Cinquefoil with five-fingered, silky-haired leaves and loose clusters of white flowers on stems that hang from rock faces. Grows in crevices of sunny limestone and dolomite cliffs.

Primula auricula.d: Primrose with thick, fleshy, mealy-edged leaves and umbels of fragrant, bright yellow flowers. Grows in crevices of limestone and dolomite cliffs.

Rhamnus pumila.d: Creeping shrub pressed flat against rock, with oval, finely toothed leaves and black berries. Grows on limestone cliffs.

Saxifraga mutata.d: Saxifrage with large rosettes of fleshy leaves with white-crusted margins and tall panicles of narrow orange flowers. Grows on moist, shaded rocks and marly slopes.

Saxifraga paniculata.d: Saxifrage with rosettes of leaves with lime-encrusted teeth and white flowers. Grows in rock crevices.

Silene saxifraga.d: Small, tufted plant with narrow leaves and single white flowers, reddish outside, opening in the evening. Grows in limestone crevices.

Valeriana saxatilis.d: Small valerian with narrow, three-veined basal leaves and small white flower clusters. Grows in crevices of limestone and dolomite cliffs.

Woodsia pulchella.d: Small, delicate fern with hairless fronds. Grows in limestone crevices; South Tyrol bears special responsibility for it.

Asplenium septentrionale.d: Small fern with grass-like, forked fronds that end in narrow, toothed segments. Grows only in crevices of acidic rock (granite, porphyry, schist).

Primula hirsuta.d: Low primrose with sticky, glandular-hairy leaves and pink flowers with a white eye. Grows in crevices of siliceous rocks.

Saxifraga exarata.d: Soft cushions of three-lobed leaves with furrows; white or cream flowers. Grows on siliceous rocks and scree.

Woodsia alpina.d: Small, tufted fern with short, pinnate fronds and rounded leaflets. Grows in crevices of siliceous rocks.

Cerastium carinthiacum.d: Loose, creeping mouse-ear with glossy, nearly hairless leaves and large, pure white flowers. Grows on fine limestone and dolomite scree in the subalpine and alpine belts.

Festuca pulchella subsp. jurana.d: Loosely tufted fescue with soft, flat, glossy leaves and loose panicles of shiny, violet-tinged spikelets. Grows on moist, fine limestone scree in the subalpine and alpine belts.

Linaria alpina.d: Prostrate plant with blue-grey, succulent leaves and violet flowers with a bright orange spot on the lip. Grows on limestone scree and river gravels.

Noccaea rotundifolia.d: Low, creeping crucifer with rounded, fleshy leaves and fragrant lilac flowers. Grows on limestone scree.

Papaver alpinum.d: Low poppy with finely cut leaves and white or yellow flowers. Grows on limestone scree.

Ranunculus parnassifolius.d: Buttercup with heart-shaped, undivided, woolly-veined leaves and white or pinkish flowers. A rare plant of moist limestone scree; endangered.

Saxifraga moschata.d: Loose cushion of divided leaves with yellowish or reddish flowers. Grows on calcareous scree and rocks.

Saxifraga oppositifolia.d: Mat-forming saxifrage with tiny, opposite, lime-crusted leaves and large purple flowers that open soon after snowmelt. Grows on high-alpine scree and rocks.

Saxifraga sedoides.d: Small, loose cushions of fleshy, stonecrop-like leaves with tiny yellowish flowers with narrow petals. Grows on moist limestone scree in shady spots.

Scorzoneroides montana.d: Hawkbit with a rosette of toothed, almost hairless leaves and single golden heads on short stems. Grows on fine limestone scree.

Valeriana supina.d: Tiny, mat-forming valerian with spoon-shaped leaves and dense heads of pink flowers. Grows on fine limestone and dolomite scree.

Adenostyles alpina.d: Smaller relative of the grey alpine butterbur with glossy, regularly toothed leaves that are green and almost hairless beneath. Grows on moist limestone scree and in spruce and larch woods.

Dryopteris villarii.d: Fern with stiff, glandular fronds that smell of balsam when crushed. Grows on limestone scree and boulder fields.

Gymnocarpium robertianum.d: Fern with triangular, glandular, slightly mealy fronds on long stalks. Grows on limestone scree, walls and rocky slopes.

Leontodon hispidus subsp. hyoseroides.it: Dente di leone a foglie divise
Leontodon hispidus subsp. hyoseroides.d: Hawkbit with deeply and regularly cut, almost hairless leaves and single golden heads on leafless stems. Grows on moving, coarse limestone scree.

Poa cenisia.d: Grass spreading with long, creeping runners and loose violet panicles. Grows on moist limestone scree.

Rumex scutatus.d: Sprawling, bluish-green perennial with fleshy, shield- or violin-shaped leaves and pink-winged fruits. Grows on limestone and siliceous scree and walls.

Trisetum distichophyllum.d: Creeping grass with short, stiff, bluish leaves in two rows and shiny yellow-brown panicles. Grows on moving limestone scree.

Valeriana montana.d: Valerian with glossy, undivided, oval leaves and dense clusters of pink flowers. Grows on moist limestone scree and in larch woods.

Achillea nana.d: Low, densely woolly-white yarrow with finely divided leaves and tight heads of whitish flowers. Strong aromatic smell. Grows on moving calcschist scree and moraines in the high-alpine belt.

Artemisia genipi.d: Small, silvery-hairy wormwood with an unbranched spike of dark, nodding flower heads. Highly aromatic. Grows on high-alpine calcschist scree.

Campanula cenisia.d: Tiny, creeping bellflower with rosettes of pale leaves and upturned, star-like blue flowers. Grows on high-alpine calcschist scree.

Comastoma tenellum.d: Tiny annual gentian, 2-10 cm, with single, pale blue, four-lobed flowers fringed with hairs inside the throat. Grows on wind-swept ridges and calcschist scree.

Crepis rhaetica.d: Small, rosette-forming hawk's-beard with pinnately lobed leaves and single yellow heads. Restricted to high-alpine calcschist scree; endangered in South Tyrol.

Doronicum glaciale.d: Low leopard's-bane with glandular leaves and single yellow heads. Grows on calcschist and limestone scree high in the Alps.

Draba dolomitica.d: Tiny, dense cushion of star-hairy rosettes topped by small white flowers. An endemic of the high Dolomites, growing in crevices and on scree.

Draba fladnizensis.d: Small, loose cushion of fringed rosettes with white flowers on short leafless stems. Grows on high-alpine scree and wind-swept ridges.

Draba hoppeana.d: Tiny, dense cushion of bristly-fringed rosettes with bright yellow flowers on very short stems. Grows on high-alpine calcschist scree; South Tyrol bears special responsibility for it.

Gentiana orbicularis.d: Small gentian with rounded, overlapping leaves and deep blue star flowers. Grows on high-alpine calcschist scree and ridges.

Herniaria alpina.d: Prostrate, cushion-forming plant with tiny, fringed leaves and minute greenish flowers. Grows on high-alpine calcschist scree.

Hornungia alpina subsp. brevicaulis.d: Small crucifer with glossy, pinnate leaves and dense heads of white flowers on very short stems. Grows on high-alpine calcschist scree.

Pedicularis aspleniifolia.d: Low lousewort with fern-like, pinnate leaves and a short head of pink-purple, hooded flowers. An eastern Alpine plant of calcschist scree and damp alpine turf.

Saxifraga biflora.d: Loose, creeping saxifrage with fleshy, hairy leaves and pairs of purple-violet flowers. Grows on wet, high-alpine calcschist scree.

Sesleria ovata.d: Small, tufted grass with a short, oval, few-flowered bluish spike. Grows on high-alpine calcschist scree.

Taraxacum pacheri.d: Small dandelion with narrow, almost entire leaves and pale yellow heads with erect outer bracts. Grows on high-alpine calcschist scree; vulnerable.

Trisetum spicatum.d: Small, tufted grass with a dense, spike-like, dark violet panicle. Grows on high-alpine scree and wind-swept ridges.

Achnatherum calamagrostis.d: Robust tussock grass with long, silvery, gently nodding panicles whose spikelets carry a short awn. Forms loose stands on warm, dry limestone scree and road cuttings at low altitude.

Centranthus angustifolius.d: Valerian with narrow, bluish leaves and dense clusters of pink spurred flowers. Very rare on warm limestone scree.

Clinopodium nepeta agg..d: Strongly aromatic, mint-scented perennial with small, grey-green leaves and loose clusters of pale lilac flowers in late summer. Grows on warm, dry scree, walls and rocky slopes.

Galeopsis angustifolia.d: Annual hemp-nettle with narrow, almost untoothed leaves and bright pink-purple flowers with a white-and-yellow-marked lip. Grows on warm limestone scree, gravels and rail tracks.

Laserpitium siler.d: Hairless umbellifer with bluish, leathery, narrow leaflets and large white umbels. Grows on warm limestone slopes, scree and forest fringes.

Androsace alpina.d: Loose cushion plant with small hairy rosettes and pink or white flowers with a yellow eye. One of the highest-climbing flowering plants, growing on siliceous scree near glaciers.

Athyrium distentifolium.d: Large fern similar to lady-fern but with rounded sori lacking a cover. Forms stands in moist subalpine tall-herb vegetation, green alder scrub and boulder fields.

Cardamine resedifolia.d: Small, tufted crucifer with pinnate leaves and white flowers. Grows on siliceous scree and rock ledges up to the highest summits.

Cerastium pedunculatum.d: Low, creeping mouse-ear with soft, hairy leaves and large white flowers on stalks much longer than the leaves. Grows on moist siliceous scree and in snowbeds high in the Alps.

Cerastium uniflorum.d: Forms low, cushion-like mats of small, hairy leaves topped by single, large white flowers. Grows on moving siliceous scree and moraines up to the highest altitudes.

Cryptogramma crispa.d: Fern with bright green, parsley-like sterile fronds and taller fertile fronds with narrow, rolled segments. Grows on acidic, moist block scree in the subalpine and alpine belts.

Doronicum clusii.d: Low leopard's-bane with soft, hairy, toothed leaves and single large golden-yellow flower heads. Grows on moist siliceous scree in the alpine belt.

Geum reptans.d: Avens with pinnate leaves, long red runners and large golden flowers; feathery fruits. Grows on siliceous scree near glaciers.

Luzula alpinopilosa.d: Wood-rush with nearly hairless leaves and loose clusters of dark brown flowers. Grows in snowbeds and on moist siliceous scree.

Oxyria digyna.d: Hairless plant with long-stalked, kidney-shaped, slightly fleshy leaves and loose clusters of round, red-winged fruits. Grows on moist siliceous scree and in late-snow spots.

Poa laxa.d: Small, delicate grass with narrow leaves and a loose panicle of a few violet spikelets. Grows on moist siliceous scree high in the alpine belt.

Ranunculus glacialis.d: Fleshy buttercup with deeply divided leaves and large white flowers that turn pink-red with age. Grows on siliceous scree near glaciers, up to over 4,000 m in the Alps.

Saxifraga bryoides.d: Dense, moss-like cushion with tiny leaves and pale yellow flowers spotted orange. Grows on siliceous scree and rocks.

Saxifraga seguieri.d: Small rosette saxifrage with spoon-shaped leaves and tiny yellowish flowers. Grows on siliceous scree and in acidic snowbeds.

Atocion rupestre.d: Small, hairless silene with forked stems and many small white or pinkish flowers. Grows in crevices and on shallow soils over acidic rock.

Epilobium collinum.d: Small, bushy willowherb with grey-green leaves and small pale pink flowers. Grows on stony siliceous slopes and walls.

Galeopsis ladanum.d: Annual hemp-nettle with broader, toothed leaves and pink-purple flowers. Grows on siliceous scree, stony fields and disturbed ground.

Galeopsis tetrahit.d: Bristly annual with stems swollen below the nodes and pink, purple or white flowers. Common in clearings, field edges and disturbed ground.

Sedum album.d: Mat-forming stonecrop with cylindrical, often reddish leaves and flat clusters of white flowers. Grows on rocks, walls and dry outcrops.

Dianthus sylvestris.d: Tufted pink with grassy, bluish leaves and single pink flowers with shallowly toothed petals. Grows on dry, rocky slopes and in sunny grasslands.

Dryas octopetala.d: Creeping dwarf shrub with small, oak-like leaves white beneath and large white flowers with eight petals; feathery seed heads. Very common on limestone.

Globularia cordifolia.d: Creeping dwarf shrub with notched, spoon-shaped leaves and blue flower balls on short stalks. Grows on limestone rocks and in calcareous heaths.

Helianthemum alpestre.d: Low, creeping dwarf shrub with small, nearly hairless leaves and bright yellow flowers. Grows on wind-swept limestone and dolomite ridges.

Sempervivum tectorum.d: Houseleek with large, red-tipped rosettes and pink flowers on tall, leafy stems. Grows on rocks and old walls.

Sesleria caerulea.d: Tufted grass with an oval, blue-grey spike that appears early in spring. Dominates calcareous grasslands and rocky slopes.

Alyssum alyssoides.d: Grey-hairy annual, 5-20 cm, with tiny pale-yellow flowers fading to white and round, hairy pods. Grows on open, dry, sunny rock outcrops and shallow soils.

Bombycilaena erecta.d: Tiny, woolly-white annual with small rounded flower heads hidden in wool. A very rare plant of open, dry limestone outcrops in the warmest valleys.

Cerastium brachypetalum.d: Small annual, densely grey-hairy, with tiny white flowers whose petals are shorter than the sepals. Grows on open, dry rock outcrops and sandy soils in the warmest valleys.

Cerastium semidecandrum.d: Tiny, sticky-hairy annual with small white flowers; the bracts have broad, papery, silvery margins. One of the first spring annuals on dry, sandy outcrops.

Draba verna agg..d: Tiny annual with a basal rosette and small white flowers with deeply split petals; flat, oval pods. One of the first spring flowers on dry outcrops.

Minuartia hybrida.d: Tiny, slender annual with thread-like leaves and small white flowers whose petals are shorter than the sepals. Critically endangered on dry, open limestone outcrops.

Minuartia rubra.d: Small annual with upright, tightly clustered stems and tiny white flowers. Grows on dry, open rock outcrops at low altitude.

Poa molinerii.d: Tufted grass with narrow, grey-green leaves and a dense, contracted panicle. Grows in dry grasslands, on rock outcrops and under rock shelters.

Saxifraga tridactylites.d: Small, glandular annual, often reddish, with three-lobed leaves and tiny white flowers in spring. Grows on dry rock outcrops and walls.

Sedum sexangulare.d: Low stonecrop with tiny, cylindrical leaves in six spiral rows and yellow flowers. Grows on dry rocks and sandy soils.

Cerastium arvense subsp. strictum.d: Mat-forming mouse-ear with narrow, almost hairless leaves and relatively large white flowers with deeply notched petals. Grows on dry, rocky siliceous slopes and shallow soils from the montane to the alpine belt.

Minuartia laricifolia.d: Loose, creeping perennial with needle-like leaves resembling larch tufts and large white flowers. Grows on dry, rocky siliceous slopes.

Plantago strictissima.d: Plantain with narrow, fleshy leaves in dense rosettes and short flower spikes. Grows on dry siliceous and serpentine rocks.

Scleranthus perennis.d: Small perennial with narrow leaves and green flowers with white margins. Grows on dry siliceous rocks.

Sedum annuum.d: Small, branched annual stonecrop with short, plump leaves and yellow star flowers. Grows on dry siliceous rocks.

Sempervivum arachnoideum.d: Houseleek with small rosettes covered with cobweb-like white hairs and bright pink flowers. Grows on siliceous rocks.

Sempervivum montanum.d: Houseleek with small, glandular-hairy rosettes and purple-red flowers. Grows on siliceous rocks and in alpine grasslands.

Veronica dillenii.d: Small, glandular annual speedwell with deeply cut leaves and deep blue flowers. Grows on dry, sandy siliceous soils.

Aira caryophyllea.d: Tiny annual grass, 5-25 cm, with spreading, airy panicles of silvery spikelets on hair-fine stalks. A rarity of shallow, sun-baked siliceous soils in the lowest valleys.

Aira elegantissima.d: Very slender annual grass whose spikelets sit on long, capillary stalks, giving a cloud-like panicle. Grows on dry, acidic rock outcrops at low altitude; critically endangered in South Tyrol.

Arabidopsis thaliana.d: Small annual, 5-30 cm, with a basal rosette, tiny white flowers and long narrow pods. The famous lab plant; in the wild it grows on open, sandy or rocky soils.

Cruciata pedemontana.d: Tiny, hairy annual with whorls of four small leaves and minute yellow flowers hidden in the leaf axils. Grows on dry, acidic rock outcrops at low altitude.

Filago minima.d: Slender, silvery-woolly annual, 5-15 cm, with tiny conical flower heads in small clusters. A rare plant of dry, sandy siliceous outcrops at low altitude.

Myosotis ramosissima.d: Small, hairy annual with tiny sky-blue flowers on branched stems. Grows on dry, sandy siliceous outcrops.

Myosotis stricta.d: Tiny annual with minute blue flowers crowded at the stem tips. Grows on dry outcrops and under rock shelters.

Poa bulbosa.d: Small grass with a swollen, bulb-like base and spikelets that often produce plantlets. Grows on dry, shallow soils and rock outcrops.

Potentilla argentea.d: Low cinquefoil with five-fingered leaves white-felted beneath and small yellow flowers. Grows on dry, sandy siliceous soils.

Scleranthus annuus agg..d: Small annual with narrow leaves and clusters of green flowers with pointed sepals. Grows on dry, sandy soils and outcrops.

Veronica verna.d: Tiny annual speedwell with deeply lobed leaves and minute blue flowers in spring. Grows on dry, sandy soils and outcrops.

Vicia lathyroides.d: Small, delicate vetch with single purple flowers in the leaf axils. Grows on dry, sandy soils.

Arabis ciliata.d: Slender crucifer with a rosette of fringed leaves and small white flowers on an upright stem. Grows in calcareous alpine grasslands with blue moor-grass.

Carex sempervirens.d: Tufted sedge with narrow leaves and a base wrapped in persistent, straw-coloured old sheaths; dark brown spikes with pale margins. One of the commonest grasses-like plants in calcareous alpine grasslands.

Gentiana clusii.d: Trumpet gentian with stiff, pointed, leathery leaves and large, deep blue trumpets without green spots inside. Grows in calcareous alpine grasslands; the limestone counterpart of trumpet gentian.

Gentiana verna.d: Small gentian with a flat leaf rosette and single, brilliant sky-blue star flowers in spring. Common in calcareous grasslands and pastures.

Hieracium pilosum.d: Hawkweed with leaves covered in long, soft hairs and single large yellow heads. Grows in calcareous alpine grasslands.

Hieracium villosum.d: Hawkweed densely covered with long, white hairs, with large yellow heads and broad, hairy bracts. Grows in calcareous alpine grasslands.

Leontopodium alpinum.d: Woolly-white plant, 5-20 cm, whose small flower heads sit in a star of thick, white-felted bracts. Grows on calcareous alpine grasslands and rock ledges; a symbol of the Alps.

Oxytropis montana agg..d: Low, tufted legume with pinnate leaves and dense heads of purple-violet flowers whose keel ends in a small point. Grows in calcareous alpine grasslands.

Primula halleri.d: Primrose with mealy leaves and pink-lilac flowers on a very long, slender corolla tube. Grows in calcareous alpine grasslands.

Carex firma.d: Builds firm, dense cushions of short, rigid, glossy dark-green leaves; short stems with a single male spike above stalked female spikes. A pioneer on wind-swept limestone and dolomite ridges, giving its name to the cushion-sedge swards.

Chamorchis alpina.d: Tiny orchid, 5-12 cm, with grass-like leaves overtopping a short spike of greenish-brown flowers. Grows on wind-swept limestone ridges and in cushion-sedge swards.

Crepis jacquinii subsp. kerneri.d: Low hawk's-beard with deeply pinnatifid leaves and one or few yellow flower heads. Grows in cushion-sedge swards and on limestone rocks in the alpine belt.

Gentianella engadinensis.d: Annual gentian with branched stems and violet, five-lobed flowers fringed inside the throat. Grows on calcareous alpine grasslands; South Tyrol bears special responsibility for it.

Pedicularis rostratocapitata.d: Lousewort with pinnate leaves and a compact head of pink flowers whose upper lip ends in a long beak. Grows on calcareous alpine grasslands and cushion-sedge swards.

Saxifraga caesia.d: Small, grey-blue cushions dotted with lime pores; white flowers on thin stems. Grows on limestone rocks and cushion-sedge swards.

Astragalus frigidus.d: Upright milk-vetch with pinnate leaves of broad, bluish-green leaflets and racemes of pale yellow flowers. Grows in rich calcareous grasslands with rusty sedge.

Bellidiastrum michelii.d: Daisy-like plant with a basal rosette of toothed leaves and single white flower heads on a leafless stem. Grows in moist calcareous grasslands and open conifer woods.

Calamagrostis varia.d: Tufted grass with violet-tinged, glossy panicles. Dominates tall-grass slopes on limestone and is common in pine and larch woods.

Carex ferruginea.d: Loosely tufted sedge with drooping, rust-brown spikes on slender stalks. Forms swards on moist, deep calcareous soils in the subalpine belt.

Festuca nigricans.d: Loosely tufted fescue with flat, soft leaves and loose panicles of dark violet, almost blackish spikelets. Grows in moist, deep-soiled alpine grasslands on both limestone and silicate.

Festuca norica.d: Tufted fescue with flat leaves and loose, nodding panicles of violet spikelets. An eastern Alpine species of rusty-sedge swards on moist calcareous slopes.

Festuca pulchella subsp. pulchella.d: Fescue with soft, flat, bright-green leaves and glossy, violet-brown spikelets in a lax panicle. Grows on moist, long-snow calcareous slopes with rusty sedge.

Lathyrus laevigatus subsp. occidentalis.d: Upright pea with pinnate leaves of broad leaflets and racemes of pale yellow flowers turning brownish. Grows in moist calcareous grasslands with rusty sedge.

Mutellina adonidifolia.d: Small umbellifer with finely dissected, aromatic leaves and pinkish-white umbels. A valued forage plant of fertile alpine pastures.

Pedicularis foliosa.d: Tall lousewort, 20-50 cm, with fern-like leaves and a dense, leafy spike of pale sulphur-yellow flowers. Grows in rich calcareous grasslands with rusty sedge.

Pedicularis rostratospicata.d: Lousewort with pinnate leaves and long, loose spikes of flesh-pink flowers whose upper lip ends in a short beak. Grows in rich calcareous grasslands; endangered.

Traunsteinera globosa.d: Slender orchid whose small pink flowers, with spotted, three-lobed lips, form a dense, rounded to conical head. Grows in calcareous grasslands with rusty sedge and in mountain meadows.

Trifolium badium.d: Clover whose heads open golden-yellow and turn chestnut-brown as they age. Grows in fertile alpine pastures and moist calcareous grasslands.

Antennaria carpatica.d: Woolly cushion plant with narrow, grey-felted leaves and small clusters of dark brown flower heads. No runners. Grows on wind-exposed calcareous ridges.

Dianthus glacialis.d: Dense cushion of short, grassy leaves with single, short-stalked pink flowers. An eastern Alpine pink of wind-swept ridges and short alpine turf.

Draba siliquosa.d: Small rosette plant with star-hairy leaves and white flowers. Grows on wind-swept alpine ridges and in alpine turf.

Gentiana brachyphylla.d: Small gentian with short, rhombic leaves in a rosette and deep blue star flowers on short stems. Grows on wind-swept, acidic and calcareous alpine ridges.

Gentiana nivalis.d: Tiny annual gentian, 3-15 cm, with small, deep blue star flowers that open only in sunshine. Grows in short alpine grasslands and on ridges.

Gentiana prostrata.d: Tiny gentian with prostrate stems and single sky-blue flowers that close within seconds when shaded. Grows on wind-swept alpine ridges; South Tyrol bears special responsibility for it.

Kobresia myosuroides.d: Densely tufted sedge with hair-fine leaves and a slender, mouse-tail spike. Dominates wind-swept ridges where snow is blown away.

Potentilla nivea.d: Low cinquefoil with trifoliate leaves densely white-felted beneath and bright yellow flowers. Grows on wind-swept calcareous ridges; vulnerable.

Saussurea alpina.d: Low plant with lance-shaped leaves woolly beneath and clusters of purple flower heads. Grows on wind-swept alpine ridges.

Avenula pratensis agg..d: Tufted grass with stiff, bluish-grey leaves and narrow panicles of large, shiny awned spikelets. Grows in dry grasslands and on sunny siliceous alpine slopes.

Festuca paniculata.d: Robust, tussock-forming fescue with broad leaves and golden panicles. Grows on sunny siliceous slopes of the subalpine belt.

Festuca varia.d: Forms large, hard, prickly tussocks of stiff, sharp leaves with violet-and-gold spikelets. Dominates steep, sunny siliceous slopes in the subalpine belt; an eastern Alpine endemic.

Laserpitium halleri.d: Umbellifer, 20-50 cm, with finely divided, fern-like, hairy leaves and white umbels with many rays. Grows on sunny, stony siliceous slopes and in variegated fescue swards.

Poa variegata.d: Tufted grass with narrow leaves and violet, variegated spikelets. Grows on sunny, acidic subalpine slopes.

Sempervivum wulfenii.d: Houseleek with large, bluish-green rosettes and pale yellow flowers with a purple spot at the base. Grows on sunny siliceous slopes.

Agrostis agrostiflora.d: Small, delicate grass with fine leaves and narrow, often violet panicles; the spikelets lack a palea. Grows in moist, long-snow siliceous grasslands, tall-herb stands and snowy hollows.

Androsace obtusifolia.d: Small rosette plant with blunt, nearly hairless leaves and umbels of white or pale pink flowers on a short stem. Grows in acidic alpine grasslands with curved sedge.

Carex curvula.d: Tufted sedge with curled, dying leaf tips that give swards a brownish look. Dominates acidic alpine grasslands above 2,300 m.

Festuca halleri.d: Low, dense fescue with bristle-fine, grey-green leaves and small, compact panicles of violet-tinged spikelets. Grows in short, acidic alpine grasslands with curved sedge and on wind-exposed heaths.

Hieracium glanduliferum.d: Low hawkweed with long-haired leaves and a single yellow head on a glandular stem. Grows in acidic alpine grasslands.

Juncus trifidus.d: Densely tufted rush with three thread-like leaves at the top of each stem and a few brown flowers. Grows on wind-swept acidic alpine ridges.

Minuartia recurva.d: Dense cushion of curved, sickle-shaped, three-veined leaves topped by small white flowers. Grows in acidic alpine grasslands and on rock ledges.

Oreochloa disticha.d: Small, densely tufted grass with bristle-fine leaves and a short, flattened spike of violet spikelets in two rows. Grows on wind-swept acidic alpine ridges with curved sedge.

Pedicularis kerneri.d: Low lousewort with pinnate leaves and a few large, pink-red flowers with a long beak. Grows in acidic alpine grasslands on silicate.

Phyteuma globulariifolium.d: Tiny rampion, 2-5 cm, with small spoon-shaped leaves and a round head of a few deep blue flowers. Grows on wind-swept acidic alpine ridges.

Potentilla frigida.d: Tiny, densely hairy cinquefoil with trifoliate leaves and small pale yellow flowers. Grows on acidic, high-alpine ridges and rocky turf.

Primula minima.d: Tiny primrose with wedge-shaped, glossy, toothed leaves and single large pink flowers with deeply notched petals. Grows in acidic alpine grasslands.

Pulsatilla vernalis.d: Low pasqueflower with evergreen leaves and white flowers covered outside with golden-brown hairs. Grows in acidic alpine grasslands.

Scorzoneroides helvetica.d: Hawkbit with hairy leaves and single golden heads. Grows in acidic mat-grass pastures and alpine grasslands.

Veronica bellidioides.d: Low speedwell with a rosette of hairy, daisy-like leaves and a short spike of deep blue flowers. Grows in acidic alpine grasslands.

Ajuga pyramidalis.d: Low plant with a dense pyramid of pale violet flowers half hidden among large, often purplish bracts. No runners. Grows in acidic mat-grass pastures and heaths.

Arnica montana.d: Rosette of opposite, hairy leaves and orange-yellow flower heads on a stem with 1-2 pairs of small leaves. Medicinal. Grows in acidic mat-grass pastures; declines with fertilisation.

Avenella flexuosa.d: Tufted grass with very fine, bristle-like leaves and airy, shining panicles on wavy stalks. Indicator of acidic, nutrient-poor soils in woods and heaths.

Botrychium lunaria.d: Small fern with one leathery, pinnate frond of half-moon-shaped leaflets and a separate fertile spike. Grows in nutrient-poor mountain pastures.

Campanula barbata.d: Bellflower with a one-sided cluster of pale blue, nodding bells fringed with long hairs inside. Grows in acidic mat-grass pastures and heaths.

Coeloglossum viride.d: Small orchid, 5-25 cm, with greenish to reddish-brown flowers; the hanging, strap-shaped lip ends in three teeth, the middle one shortest. Grows in nutrient-poor pastures and alpine grasslands.

Festuca nigrescens.d: Densely tufted red fescue without runners; fine, rolled leaves and narrow, reddish-violet panicles. Common in mat-grass pastures, mountain meadows and nutrient-poor grasslands.

Gentiana acaulis.d: Low gentian with large, deep blue, trumpet flowers on very short stems. Grows in acidic mat-grass pastures and heaths.

Gentiana punctata.d: Tall gentian, 20-60 cm, with broad, ribbed leaves and pale yellow bell flowers densely spotted with purple. Grows in acidic mat-grass pastures and heaths.

Geum montanum.d: Low plant with pinnate leaves with a large end lobe and golden flowers; feathery fruits. Grows in acidic mat-grass pastures.

Hypochaeris uniflora.d: Hairy plant with a single large, golden-yellow head on a stem that is clearly swollen just below the head; bracts with black hairs. Grows in acidic mat-grass pastures.

Luzula alpina.d: Small wood-rush with hairy, grass-like leaves and dense, dark brown flower heads. Grows in mat-grass pastures.
