Nardus stricta.d: Dense, wiry tussock grass with bristle-like leaves and a thin, one-sided spike. Dominates acidic, nutrient-poor pastures.

Nigritella rhellicani.d: Small orchid with a dense, cone-shaped head of dark red-brown flowers smelling of vanilla. Grows in mountain pastures.

Pseudorchis albida.d: Small orchid with a dense spike of tiny, creamy white, fragrant flowers. Grows in acidic mat-grass pastures.

Pulsatilla alpina subsp. apiifolia.d: Pasqueflower with finely cut leaves, large pale sulphur-yellow flowers and feathery fruits. Grows in acidic mountain pastures.

Arabis caerulea.d: Small, sparsely leaved crucifer with pale blue-violet flowers and rosettes of wedge-shaped, toothed leaves. Typical of calcareous snowbeds.

Carex parviflora.d: Small, soft-leaved sedge with 2-3 short, dark brown to blackish spikes close together at the stem tip. Grows in calcareous snowbeds and damp hollows on calcschist.

Gentiana bavarica.d: Small gentian with yellowish-green, box-like, rounded leaves and single deep blue star-shaped flowers. Grows in calcareous snowbeds and along alpine rivulets.

Gnaphalium hoppeanum.d: Small, silvery-woolly cudweed with a short spike of dark brown flower heads. Grows in calcareous snowbeds and on damp alpine scree.

Potentilla brauneana.d: Tiny cinquefoil with trifoliate, almost hairless leaves and small yellow flowers on short stems. Grows in calcareous snowbeds and damp alpine turf.

Salix reticulata.d: Creeping dwarf willow with rounded leaves marked by a deeply sunken network of veins. Grows in calcareous snowbeds.

Salix retusa.d: Creeping dwarf willow with small, glossy, obovate leaves notched at the tip and short catkins. Grows in calcareous snowbeds and on scree.

Saxifraga androsacea.d: Small saxifrage with flat rosettes of spoon-shaped, hairy leaves and a few white flowers on short stems. Grows in snowbeds on limestone and calcschist.

Alchemilla pentaphyllea.d: Small, creeping lady's mantle whose leaves are cut to the base into five narrow, toothed segments. A typical plant of long-lasting snowbeds on acidic soil.

Cardamine alpina.d: Tiny crucifer with rounded basal leaves and small white flowers. Grows in acidic snowbeds where snow lies until mid-summer.

Carex foetida.d: Low sedge with soft leaves and a single, compact, dark brown head; the crushed rhizome smells unpleasant. Grows in acidic snowbeds and wet hollows where snow lies until July.

Carex lachenalii.d: Low sedge with 2-4 short brown spikes near the stem tip. Grows in acidic snowbeds and wet stony soils.

Gnaphalium supinum.d: Tiny, mat-forming, woolly cudweed with a few small brown heads. Grows in acidic snowbeds where snow lies late.

Salix herbacea.d: One of the smallest woody plants: creeping underground stems send up just a couple of round, glossy leaves. Grows in acidic snowbeds.

Sibbaldia procumbens.d: Low plant with bluish trifoliate leaves whose leaflets end in three teeth, and tiny yellow flowers. Grows in acidic snowbeds.

Soldanella pusilla.d: Tiny plant with small, round leaves and single, pale violet, fringed bells. Grows in acidic snowbeds, often flowering through melting snow.

Anthericum ramosum.d: Grass-leaved perennial with a branched inflorescence of small, star-like white flowers. Common on warm, dry slopes, fringes and light pine woods.

Bromus erectus.d: Tufted grass with upright panicles of reddish spikelets and fringed basal leaves. The leading grass of semi-dry grasslands on limestone.

Gymnadenia odoratissima.d: Slender orchid with a dense, cylindrical spike of small, vanilla-scented pale pink flowers. Grows in calcareous grasslands, fens and light pine woods.

Laserpitium latifolium.d: Tall umbellifer up to 1.5 m with large, bluish, heart-shaped and toothed leaflets and broad white umbels. Grows on calcareous slopes, in tall-grass stands and light woods.

Molinia arundinacea.d: Very tall tussock grass with long panicles and a bulb-like stem base. Dominates abandoned, moist slopes and light pine woods.

Adenostyles alliariae.d: Tall herb with large, heart-shaped, irregularly toothed leaves, grey-felted beneath, and dense flat clusters of pinkish-purple flower heads. A leading species of subalpine tall-herb stands and green alder scrub.

Calamagrostis arundinacea.d: Tall grass with broad leaves and dense, glossy panicles; the spikelets have a long bent awn. Grows in acidic woodland clearings and tall-grass stands on silicate.

Calamagrostis villosa.d: Grass with soft, hairy leaf sheaths and loose purplish panicles. Forms carpets under subalpine spruce and stone pine forests on acidic soil.

Epilobium angustifolium.d: Tall perennial with narrow, willow-like leaves and long spikes of bright pink-purple flowers; fluffy seeds. Typical of woodland clearings and burnt ground.

Luzula luzuloides.d: Tufted wood-rush with hairy leaves and loose clusters of dirty-white flowers. Grows in acidic beech and spruce woods.

Luzula nivea.d: Tall wood-rush with long, hairy leaves and dense clusters of snow-white flowers. Grows in fir, spruce and beech woods.

Peucedanum ostruthium.d: Large, aromatic umbellifer with broad, three-parted leaves and flat white umbels. Grows in tall-herb stands and green alder scrub; once widely used as a medicinal plant.

Ranunculus platanifolius.d: Tall buttercup up to 1 m with palmately lobed leaves and many white flowers on long stalks. Grows in tall-herb stands and moist mountain woods.

Rubus idaeus.d: Shrub with upright, bristly canes, pinnate leaves white beneath and red fruits. Colonises clearings and woodland edges.

Senecio cacaliaster.d: Tall ragwort with toothed leaves and pale yellow heads without ray florets. Grows in tall-herb stands.

Senecio nemorensis.d: Tall ragwort with lance-shaped, toothed leaves and yellow heads with few rays. Grows in woods and tall-herb stands.

Sorbus aucuparia.d: Tree with pinnate leaves, white flower clusters and scarlet berries. Grows in mountain woods up to the treeline.

Brachypodium pinnatum.d: Creeping grass with broad, yellow-green leaves and a slender spike of short-stalked spikelets. Spreads in abandoned grasslands and along warm forest fringes.

Brachypodium rupestre.d: Creeping grass with stiff, narrow, glossy leaves and a slender spike of short-stalked, many-flowered spikelets. Spreads across abandoned dry grasslands and sunny slopes once mowing or grazing stops.

Koeleria pyramidata.d: Tufted grass with a pyramid-shaped, shiny panicle and broad, flat leaves fringed with hairs. Grows in semi-dry grasslands on limestone.

Ophrys spp..d: Orchids whose lip mimics a female insect to attract male pollinators. Grow in semi-dry grasslands.

Achillea tomentosa.d: Grey-hairy yarrow, 10-25 cm, with feathery leaves and flat clusters of bright yellow heads. A steppe plant of the hottest, driest slopes of the Vinschgau and similar inner-Alpine valleys.

Astragalus onobrychis.d: Spreading milk-vetch with silvery-hairy pinnate leaves and dense heads of long, purple-violet flowers. Grows on dry, steppe-like slopes of the inner valleys.

Bothriochloa ischaemum.d: Warm-season grass with finger-like clusters of hairy, purplish spikes at the stem tip. Typical of the hottest, driest grasslands and steppe slopes.

Carex humilis.d: Low sedge with fine leaves that hide the small flowering stems in early spring. Dominant in dry grasslands and light pine woods.

Carex supina.d: Small sedge spreading with a slender rhizome; stems curved, with one male spike and 1-2 small, round female spikes. A continental species of the driest steppe slopes in the Vinschgau.

Dracocephalum austriacum.d: Perennial with deeply divided leaves and large blue-violet flowers. A steppe relict known from very few dry slopes.

Ephedra helvetica.d: Leafless, broom-like shrub with jointed green twigs and small red, fleshy cones. A steppe relict on the hottest rocks of the Vinschgau and Eisack valleys.

Festuca rupicola.d: Dense tufts of grey-green, rough, furrowed leaves and narrow, compact panicles. One of the leading grasses of dry, steppe-like grasslands and light oak-pine woods.

Festuca valesiaca.d: Very dense, bluish-grey tufts of bristle-fine leaves with narrow panicles. A key grass of the continental steppe slopes of the Vinschgau and other dry inner valleys.

Koeleria macrantha.d: Tufted grass with narrow, grey-green leaves and a dense, shiny, spike-like panicle that opens briefly at flowering. A typical grass of continental steppe grasslands in the dry inner valleys.

Onosma helvetica subsp. tridentina.d: Bristly perennial with nodding clusters of pale yellow tubular flowers. A rare steppe plant of the inner valleys.

Phelipanche purpurea agg..d: Leafless parasite with a bluish stem and spikes of blue-violet flowers, growing on yarrow and other composites. Grows in dry steppe grasslands.

Phleum phleoides.d: Tufted grass whose dense, cylindrical spike bends apart into lobes when flexed; stems often purplish at the base. Grows in dry steppe grasslands and sunny oak-pine woods.

Scabiosa triandra.d: Scabious with finely divided leaves and pale lilac flower heads on long stalks. Grows in dry steppe grasslands.

Stipa capillata.d: Tufted grass with rolled leaves and very long, wavy, hair-like awns. Grows in continental steppe grasslands.

Stipa epilosa.d: Feather-grass with long, feathery awns and hairless leaf blades. Grows on steppe slopes of the inner valleys; endangered.

Stipa eriocaulis.d: Feather-grass with silvery, plume-like awns up to 25 cm that wave in the wind. Grows in steppe grasslands of the dry inner valleys.

Teucrium chamaedrys.d: Small, woody plant with oak-like, toothed leaves and pink-purple flowers. Grows on dry, sunny slopes and in light woods.

Bromus condensatus.d: Brome with a dense, contracted panicle of awned spikelets. A rare southern grass of hot, dry grasslands on limestone.

Heteropogon contortus.d: Warm-climate grass whose dark, twisted awns tangle together into a knot. Rare on the hottest, driest rocky slopes.

Kengia serotina.d: Small, wiry grass whose upper flowers stay hidden in the leaf sheaths and self-pollinate. Grows on the hottest, driest rocky slopes.

Cerastium fontanum.d: Hairy, loosely tufted perennial with dull green leaves and small white flowers whose petals are deeply notched. Common in pastures and meadows; tolerant of grazing and trampling.

Crepis aurea.d: Small plant with a basal rosette of shiny leaves and a single, striking orange flower head on a black-hairy stem. Grows in fertile, grazed mountain pastures.

Phleum rhaeticum.d: Grass with a short, thick, dark violet, cylindrical spike bristling with short awns. A good forage grass of fertile alpine pastures and mountain meadows.

Poa alpina.d: Tufted grass with short, broad leaves; its spikelets often sprout small plantlets instead of seeds. An excellent forage grass of alpine pastures.

Trifolium pratense.d: Clover with stalkless pink-red heads framed by two leaves and leaflets marked with a pale crescent. Common in meadows from valley to subalpine.

Anthriscus sylvestris.d: Tall umbellifer with fern-like leaves, hollow furrowed stems and umbels of white flowers in late spring. Abundant in well-fertilised hay meadows and on road verges.

Arrhenatherum elatius.d: Tall grass, up to 1.5 m, with shiny, nodding panicles of two-flowered spikelets with a bent awn. The leading grass of lowland hay meadows.

Campanula patula.d: Slender, much-branched bellflower, 20-60 cm, with wide-open, funnel-shaped violet flowers on long stalks, the lobes spreading almost flat. Flowers May-July in well-managed lowland hay meadows and on sunny verges.

Crepis biennis.d: Tall, branched plant up to 1 m with pinnately lobed leaves and many bright yellow flower heads. A characteristic plant of fertile lowland hay meadows in late spring.

Dactylis glomerata.d: Robust, tufted grass with bluish leaves and spikelets crowded into dense, one-sided clusters at the ends of stiff branches. One of the most common grasses of fertile meadows.

Festuca pratensis.d: Tall grass with flat, glossy, dark green leaves and a narrow, slightly nodding panicle of many-flowered spikelets without awns. Common in fertile lowland and mountain hay meadows.

Geranium pratense.d: Tall crane's-bill with deeply divided, toothed leaves and large violet-blue flowers. A characteristic plant of fertile lowland hay meadows.

Holcus lanatus.d: Tufted grass with soft, grey-velvety leaves and sheaths striped pink at the base; dense, pale pinkish panicles. Common in damp, moderately fertilised meadows.

Homalotrichon pubescens.d: Loosely tufted grass with soft, hairy leaves and shiny, silvery-brown spikelets with bent awns. Grows in hay meadows and semi-dry grasslands.

Poa pratensis.d: Grass spreading with rhizomes, with smooth sheaths, a boat-shaped leaf tip and pyramid-shaped panicles. Common in meadows and pastures.

Poa trivialis.d: Grass with rough leaf sheaths, a long pointed ligule and spreading panicles. Common in moist, fertile meadows and wet woods.

Rhinanthus alectorolophus.d: Semi-parasitic annual with yellow flowers and a hairy, inflated calyx; seeds rattle when ripe. Grows in hay meadows.

Rumex acetosa.d: Perennial with arrow-shaped, sour-tasting leaves whose basal lobes point backwards, and loose spikes of reddish flowers. Common in fertile hay meadows.

Trisetum flavescens.d: Loosely tufted grass with soft leaves and a shiny, golden-yellow panicle of awned spikelets. Common in hay meadows.

Anthoxanthum odoratum.d: Early-flowering grass with a dense, spike-like panicle; crushed plants smell of fresh hay (coumarin). Widespread in meadows on poorer, slightly acidic soils.

Arabidopsis halleri.d: Perennial with runners, basal leaves often lobed and small white or lilac flowers. Tolerates heavy metals; common in mountain hay meadows of the inner valleys.

Centaurea pseudophrygia.d: Knapweed with large purple flower heads whose bracts end in long, curled, brown fringes that give a wig-like look. Grows in mountain hay meadows on siliceous soils.

Chaerophyllum villarsii.d: Umbellifer with finely cut, almost fern-like leaves and white umbels with long, pointed bracts below the small umbels. Grows in mountain hay meadows, green alder scrub and tall-herb stands.

Geranium sylvaticum.d: Crane's-bill with violet flowers with a white centre. A leading herb of mountain hay meadows and tall-herb stands.

Campanula bononiensis.d: Tall bellflower with downy leaves grey beneath and a long spike of small violet bells. A rare plant of warm, dry forest fringes.

Cervaria rivini.d: Stout umbellifer with stiff, bluish-green, twice-pinnate leaves whose leaflets are sharply toothed; white umbels in late summer. Grows along warm, dry forest fringes and in light oak and pine woods.

Clematis recta.d: Non-climbing clematis, 50-150 cm, with pinnate, bluish leaves and dense clusters of fragrant, star-like white flowers followed by feathery fruits. Grows along warm, sunny forest fringes.

Coronilla coronata.d: Bushy legume with bluish-green, pinnate leaves and rounded umbels of bright yellow pea flowers. Grows along warm, dry forest fringes on limestone.

Dictamnus albus.d: Tall perennial with pinnate leaves and showy pink flowers with dark veins. The whole plant is lemon-scented and rich in volatile oils. Grows along warm forest fringes.

Fragaria viridis.d: Strawberry with silky-hairy leaves; the pale fruits stay hard and cling to the calyx, which presses against them. Grows on warm, dry fringes and sunny grasslands.

Geranium sanguineum.d: Bushy crane's-bill with deeply cut leaves and large, bright magenta flowers; leaves turn red in autumn. Grows along warm forest fringes.

Melampyrum cristatum.d: Semi-parasitic annual with a dense, four-sided spike of yellow-and-purple flowers set in comb-toothed, purplish bracts. A rare plant of warm forest fringes.

Peucedanum venetum.d: Umbellifer with leathery, bluish, much-divided leaves and white umbels. A southern species of warm, dry forest fringes.

Seseli libanotis.d: Umbellifer with ridged stems, finely divided leaves and dense white umbels with many rays. Grows along warm, dry forest fringes.

Thesium bavarum.d: Semi-parasitic perennial with narrow, three-veined leaves and loose clusters of tiny white flowers. Grows along warm forest fringes on limestone.

Trifolium alpestre.d: Clover with narrow, finely toothed leaflets and round, deep purple-red heads usually in pairs. Grows along warm forest fringes and in light oak woods.

Trifolium rubens.d: Clover with long, cylindrical, purple-red heads and narrow, finely toothed leaflets. Grows along warm, dry forest fringes.

Vicia tenuifolia.d: Climbing vetch with narrow leaflets and long racemes of blue-violet flowers. Grows along warm forest fringes.

Agrimonia eupatoria.d: Upright herb with pinnate leaves and long slender spikes of small yellow flowers; the fruits carry hooked bristles. Grows along sunny hedges and grassy forest edges.

Astragalus glycyphyllos.d: Sprawling, nearly hairless legume with large pinnate leaves and short racemes of greenish-cream flowers; curved pods. Grows along sunny forest edges.

Clinopodium vulgare.d: Hairy, softly aromatic perennial with oval leaves and dense, bristly whorls of pink-purple flowers along the stem. Grows along hedges, forest fringes and clearings.

Lathyrus heterophyllus.d: Climbing pea with winged stems; lower leaves with one pair of leaflets, upper with two or three. Pink-purple flowers. Grows along forest fringes and hedges.

Melampyrum nemorosum agg..d: Semi-parasitic annual with yellow flowers framed by strikingly violet-blue upper bracts. Grows along mesic forest fringes and in clearings.

Origanum vulgare.d: Aromatic perennial with oval leaves and dense heads of pink flowers. Grows along warm forest fringes.

Securigera varia.d: Sprawling legume with pinnate leaves and round heads of pink-and-white pea flowers on long stalks. Grows along sunny forest fringes and verges.

Trifolium medium.d: Clover with zigzag-bent stems, narrow leaflets and stalked purple-red heads. Grows along mesic forest fringes and hedges.

Vicia dumetorum.d: Climbing vetch with large, oval leaflets and racemes of reddish-purple flowers. Grows along forest fringes; vulnerable.

Vicia sylvatica.d: Climbing vetch with long racemes of white flowers veined with violet. Grows along forest fringes and clearings.

Genista germanica.d: Low, spiny shrublet with hairy twigs, simple leaves and short spikes of yellow pea flowers. Grows on acidic heaths, fringes and light pine and oak woods.

Holcus mollis.d: Grass spreading with long rhizomes, with bearded stem nodes and soft, whitish panicles whose spikelets carry a bent awn. Grows in acidic woods, fringes and clearings.

Melampyrum pratense.d: Slender semi-parasitic annual with paired, pale yellow flowers in the axils of green leaves. Common in acidic woods, heaths and fringes.

Melampyrum sylvaticum.d: Like common cow-wheat but with smaller, deep yellow flowers whose mouth is open. Grows in conifer forests and dwarf-shrub heaths.

Angelica sylvestris.d: Tall umbellifer with hollow, often purplish stems, inflated leaf sheaths and large umbels of white or pinkish flowers. Grows in wet tall-herb stands, ditches and damp woods.

Calystegia sepium.d: Climbing vine with arrow-shaped leaves and large white trumpet flowers. Covers reeds and shrubs along rivers and damp fringes.

Cuscuta europaea.d: Leafless parasite whose reddish, thread-like stems twine around nettles and other hosts, bearing dense balls of small pinkish flowers. Grows in damp riverside fringes.

Elymus caninus.d: Tufted grass with a nodding spike of long-awned spikelets and no creeping rhizomes. Grows in damp riverside fringes and moist woods.

Epilobium tetragonum.d: Willowherb with four-angled stems, narrow, stalkless leaves and small pale pink flowers. Grows along damp, disturbed fringes, ditches and riverbanks.

Eupatorium cannabinum.d: Tall herb with hemp-like, three- to five-parted leaves and dense flat clusters of pinkish flower heads. Grows in damp fringes and clearings.

Helianthus tuberosus.d: Tall perennial sunflower up to 3 m with rough leaves, yellow heads in autumn and edible tubers. Introduced from North America; invades riverbanks.

Heracleum mantegazzianum.d: Huge umbellifer up to 4 m with gigantic leaves and umbels. Introduced from the Caucasus; its sap causes severe skin burns in sunlight.

Impatiens glandulifera.d: Tall, succulent annual up to 2.5 m with reddish stems and pink-purple, helmet-shaped flowers; ripe pods explode when touched. Introduced from Asia; forms dense stands along rivers.

Rubus caesius.d: Low bramble with weak prickles, trifoliate leaves and black fruits covered with a bluish bloom. Grows in floodplain woods and damp fringes.

Silene baccifera.d: Scrambling plant with greenish-white flowers and glossy black berries. Grows along rivers and in damp fringes.

Sonchus arvensis subsp. uliginosus.d: Tall sow-thistle with spiny-edged leaves and large yellow heads. Grows in damp fringes and reedbeds.

Symphyotrichum novi-belgii agg..it: Gruppo di Astro del Nuovo Belgio

Symphytum officinale.d: Rough-hairy plant with winged stems and nodding clusters of cream or purple bell flowers. Grows in damp meadows and along rivers.

Urtica dioica.d: Perennial with toothed leaves and stinging hairs; hanging green flower tassels. Indicates nitrogen-rich soils along rivers, fringes and huts.

Chaerophyllum hirsutum.d: Umbellifer, 30-100 cm, with soft-hairy, finely divided leaves and umbels of white or pink flowers. Lines mountain streams and grows in wet tall-herb stands and alder woods.

Petasites albus.d: Large plant with huge round leaves and white flower heads in early spring. Grows along streams and in woods.

Petasites hybridus.d: Spreads into large colonies; pink flower spikes appear before the huge, rhubarb-like leaves, which are grey-downy beneath. Grows along streams and riverbanks.

Saxifraga rotundifolia.d: Saxifrage with round, toothed leaves and white flowers spotted red. Grows in tall-herb stands and moist woods.

Senecio ovatus.d: Tall ragwort with narrow, stalked leaves and yellow heads with five rays. Grows in clearings and mountain woods.

Arabis nova.d: Annual crucifer with lyre-shaped lower leaves, small white flowers and long pods. Grows under rock overhangs enriched by the droppings of chamois and ibex.

Asperugo procumbens.d: Sprawling annual borage with rough, hooked hairs and tiny blue flowers; calyx enlarges in fruit into a flattened, toothed envelope. Grows under rock shelters rich in animal droppings.

Chenopodium bonus-henricus.d: Perennial goosefoot with arrow-shaped, mealy leaves and dense, branched spikes of small green flowers. Grows on nitrogen-rich ground near huts, stables and rock shelters.

Chenopodium foliosum.d: Annual goosefoot with triangular, toothed leaves; its flower clusters swell into bright red, strawberry-like balls along the stem. Grows on nitrogen-rich ground under rock shelters used by livestock and wild ungulates.

Cynoglossum officinale.d: Grey-downy biennial with tongue-shaped leaves, dull red-purple flowers and flat nutlets covered with hooked spines. Smells of mice. Grows on nitrogen-rich ground under rock shelters.

Descurainia sophia.d: Annual crucifer, 30-80 cm, with very finely divided, grey-green leaves and tiny pale yellow flowers followed by long, slender pods. Grows under rock shelters and on nutrient-rich, disturbed ground.

Hackelia deflexa.d: Annual borage with small blue flowers and nodding fruits whose nutlets carry hooked bristles. Grows under rock shelters frequented by ungulates.

Hornungia pauciflora.d: Tiny crucifer with pinnate leaves and a few small white flowers. Grows on nitrogen-rich ground under rock shelters used by ungulates.

Arctium nemorosum.d: Tall, coarse herb with huge heart-shaped leaves and purple flower heads wrapped in hooked bracts that cling to fur. Grows in woodland clearings and along forest roads.

Atropa belladonna.d: Robust bushy herb with large oval leaves, brownish-purple bell flowers and shiny black berries. Highly poisonous. Grows in clearings of beech and mixed forest.

Bromus benekenii.d: Tall woodland brome with drooping panicles of awned spikelets and densely hairy lower leaf sheaths. Grows in base-rich beech and mixed forests and in their clearings.

Carex pilulifera.d: Tufted sedge with curved, often lax stems; the female spikes are small, round and ball-like, set just below the male spike. Grows on acidic soils in clearings, heaths and light woods.

Carex spicata.d: Sedge with a dense head of spikes and a purplish leaf base. Grows in dry clearings and wood margins.

Fragaria vesca.d: Low plant with trifoliate leaves, white flowers and small sweet red fruits. Common in clearings and forest edges.

Galeopsis speciosa.d: Bristly annual with swollen stem nodes and large pale yellow flowers with a violet patch on the lower lip. Grows in clearings and on disturbed woodland soils.

Sambucus ebulus.d: Herbaceous elder up to 2 m with pinnate leaves, white flowers smelling of almonds and black berries. Grows in clearings; poisonous.

Senecio sylvaticus.d: Sticky-hairy annual with deeply cut leaves and small, cylindrical yellow heads with tiny rolled rays. Grows in acidic woodland clearings.

Stachys alpina.d: Hairy perennial with heart-shaped, toothed leaves and whorls of dull pink-purple flowers. Grows in mountain woodland clearings.

Equisetum telmateia.d: The largest horsetail, with ivory-white stems and dense whorls of green branches. Grows on wet, calcareous slopes and spring-fed ground.

Geranium palustre.d: Crane's-bill with deeply divided leaves and magenta-purple flowers on long, bent stalks. Grows in wet tall-herb stands, ditches and alder woods.

Thalictrum lucidum.d: Tall plant with shiny, narrow leaflets and fluffy clusters of yellow flowers. Grows in wet meadows.

Aconitum lycoctonum agg..d: Tall herb with deeply lobed palmate leaves and pale yellow, hooded flowers whose helmet is much taller than wide. Very poisonous. Grows in shady tall-herb stands, green alder scrub and moist woods.

Aconitum napellus agg..d: Tall, highly poisonous plant with deeply divided leaves and dense spikes of deep violet-blue, helmet-shaped flowers. Typical of nutrient-rich tall-herb stands near alpine huts and streams.

Aconitum variegatum agg..d: Monkshood with branched, looser inflorescences of blue or blue-and-white flowers whose helmet is taller and more arched than in A. napellus. Grows in montane tall-herb stands and wood margins.

Lactuca alpina.d: Tall plant up to 2 m with lyre-shaped leaves and blue-violet flower heads in glandular clusters. Grows in subalpine tall-herb stands and green alder scrub.

Poa hybrida.d: Tall, broad-leaved meadow-grass with long, spreading panicles. Grows in subalpine tall-herb stands and green alder scrub.

Cornus sanguinea.d: Shrub with opposite, oval leaves with curved veins, flat clusters of white flowers and black berries; twigs turn blood-red in winter. Common in hedges, thickets and forest margins.

Crataegus monogyna.d: Thorny shrub or small tree with deeply lobed leaves, clusters of white flowers in May and dark red haws with a single stone. Very common in hedges and forest margins.

Prunus spinosa.d: Thorny, suckering shrub that flowers white on bare twigs in early spring; blue-black sloes. Common in hedges and thickets.

Amelanchier ovalis.d: Shrub with oval, toothed leaves woolly beneath when young and showy white flowers with narrow petals in spring. Blue-black berries. Grows in sunny rock thickets and dry pine woods.

Berberis vulgaris.d: Spiny shrub with three-parted thorns, clusters of obovate leaves and hanging yellow flowers followed by red, sour berries. Grows in sunny thickets and dry pine woods.

Colutea arborescens.d: Shrub with pinnate, bluish leaves, yellow pea flowers and conspicuous papery, inflated pods that pop when squeezed. Grows in warm, dry thickets and on rocky slopes at low altitude.

Cotoneaster tomentosus.d: Shrub with oval leaves densely white-woolly beneath, small pinkish flowers and red berries. Grows in sunny, rocky thickets and light pine woods on limestone.

Genista radiata.d: Dense, rounded shrub with opposite, three-parted leaves and yellow flowers. Grows on calcareous slopes and in pine woods.

Hippocrepis emerus.d: Shrub with green twigs, pinnate leaves and yellow pea flowers whose long claws give a spidery look; long, jointed pods. Grows in warm woods.

Ligustrum vulgare.d: Semi-evergreen shrub with narrow, untoothed, opposite leaves, dense spikes of fragrant white flowers and glossy black berries. Common in hedges and warm thickets.

Orobanche lucorum.d: Leafless, yellowish-brown parasite, 15-40 cm, with a spike of pale brownish flowers; it lives on the roots of barberry. Grows in warm, dry thickets.

Prunus mahaleb.d: Shrub with round, glossy leaves, fragrant white flowers and small black cherries. Grows in dry, warm thickets on limestone.

Rosa spp..d: Thorny shrubs with pinnate leaves, pink or white five-petalled flowers and red hips. Several species grow in sunny thickets and hedges.

Corylus avellana.d: Shrub with rounded, toothed leaves and catkins in late winter; nuts in husks. Common in hedges and woods.

Euonymus europaeus.d: Shrub with green, four-angled twigs and pink capsules that open to show orange-coated seeds. Grows in hedges and floodplain woods.

Frangula alnus.d: Shrub with untoothed, oval leaves, small greenish flowers and berries turning red then black. Grows in fens and wet woods.

Ribes uva-crispa.d: Spiny shrub with three- to five-lobed leaves and green to reddish, hairy berries. Grows in hedges, rocky thickets and floodplain woods.

Rubus spp..d: Thorny, arching shrubs with palmate leaves, white or pink flowers and black fruits. Form dense thickets in hedges and clearings.

Betula pendula.d: Pioneer tree with white peeling bark, hanging twigs and diamond-shaped, double-toothed leaves. Colonises clearings, screes and dry acidic woods.

Salix caprea.d: Shrub or small tree with broad, oval leaves grey-woolly beneath and large silver "pussy willow" catkins in early spring. A pioneer in clearings and on rubble.

Sambucus nigra.d: Shrub with corky bark, pinnate leaves, flat creamy flower heads and black berries. Common in hedges and nutrient-rich woods.

Sambucus racemosa.d: Shrub with pinnate leaves, egg-shaped clusters of yellowish flowers and scarlet berries. Grows in mountain clearings.

Alnus glutinosa.d: Tree with dark fissured bark and rounded, often notched leaves that are sticky when young. Woody cone-like fruits persist through winter. Grows in waterlogged floodplains and fens.

Betula pubescens.d: Birch with upright, hairy twigs and more rounded leaves than silver birch; bark less rugged at the base. Grows in bogs, fens and bog woodland.

Salix cinerea.d: Rounded shrub with grey-downy twigs and obovate leaves; peeled wood shows raised ridges. Forms swamp scrub at fen margins.

Alnus alnobetula.d: Shrub, 1-3 m, with sticky young twigs and finely double-toothed, glossy leaves; male catkins appear with the leaves. Forms dense, bending scrub on moist, avalanche-prone north slopes.

Daphne mezereum.d: Shrub whose fragrant pink flowers crowd along bare twigs in late winter; bright red berries in summer. All parts are highly poisonous. Grows in mountain woods and scrub.

Rhododendron ferrugineum.d: Evergreen shrub with leathery leaves rust-brown beneath and clusters of red-pink funnel flowers. Covers acidic slopes at the treeline.

Rhododendron hirsutum.d: Evergreen shrub with bright green leaves fringed with hairs along the edge (no rusty underside) and pink flower clusters. Grows on limestone and dolomite, often with mountain pine.

Salix breviserrata.d: Low, spreading shrub with glossy, finely toothed leaves and reddish catkins. Grows in subalpine willow scrub on moist calcareous ground.

Salix foetida.d: Low shrub with glossy, finely glandular-toothed leaves that smell unpleasant when crushed. Grows in subalpine willow scrub on siliceous soils.

Salix glabra.d: Shrub with glossy, hairless leaves bluish beneath. Grows in subalpine scrub and pine woods on limestone.

Salix glaucosericea.d: Shrub with leaves densely silky-hairy and bluish on both sides. Rare in subalpine willow scrub.

Salix hastata.d: Shrub with broad, oval leaves and large stipules, catkins with long hairs. Grows in subalpine willow scrub and along streams.

Salix hegetschweileri.d: Upright shrub with glossy, toothed leaves bluish beneath and dark twigs. Grows in subalpine willow scrub on wet ground; vulnerable.

Salix helvetica.d: Low shrub with leaves white-felted beneath and woolly catkins. Grows in subalpine willow scrub on siliceous soils.

Salix mielichhoferi.d: Shrub with glossy, dark green leaves and red-brown twigs. An eastern Alpine species of subalpine scrub on siliceous soils.

Salix waldsteiniana.d: Low shrub with glossy, finely toothed leaves and short catkins. Grows in subalpine scrub on calcareous soils.

Arctostaphylos alpinus.d: Creeping deciduous dwarf shrub with wrinkled, toothed leaves that turn bright red in autumn; black berries. Grows in calcareous dwarf-shrub heath and mountain pine scrub.

Arctostaphylos uva-ursi.d: Creeping evergreen dwarf shrub with leathery, untoothed, spoon-shaped leaves and red berries. Similar to cowberry but without dark dots beneath. Grows on dry, sunny slopes and in pine woods.

Daphne striata.d: Low, evergreen shrublet with narrow leaves and terminal clusters of fragrant pink flowers with fine stripes. Grows in calcareous heath and mountain pine scrub.

Erica carnea.d: Evergreen dwarf shrub with needle-like leaves in whorls and pink bell flowers from late winter. Covers the ground in pine woods and calcareous heaths.

Juniperus communis subsp. nana.d: Creeping juniper with short, curved, crowded needles banded white above and blue-black berry-like cones. Covers sunny subalpine slopes and heaths.

Larix decidua.d: Deciduous conifer with soft needles in tufts that turn golden in autumn. Forms open forests at the treeline.

Listera cordata.d: Tiny orchid, 5-20 cm, with two opposite, heart-shaped leaves and a few small reddish-green flowers. Grows hidden in moss under spruce and in bog woodland.

Picea abies.d: Tall conifer with a pointed crown, sharp four-sided needles all around the twig and long cones hanging down. The most common tree of South Tyrol, from the valleys to the treeline.

Pinus cembra.d: Pine with five soft needles per bundle and plump cones whose large seeds are eaten by nutcrackers. Forms forests with larch at the treeline.

Pinus mugo.d: Shrubby, multi-stemmed pine with paired, stiff, dark green needles and small cones. Forms dense, creeping thickets on limestone scree and avalanche tracks.

Rhodothamnus chamaecistus.d: Tiny shrub, 10-30 cm, with small, hair-fringed leaves and large, flat, pale pink flowers. An eastern Alpine plant of limestone and dolomite rocks and heaths.

Vaccinium gaultherioides.d: Low shrub with small, bluish-green, untoothed leaves and blue-black berries. Grows in alpine heaths and on wind-exposed ridges.

Sphagnum magellanicum.d: Robust peat moss with plump, wine-red heads and spoon-shaped leaves. Builds hummocks on raised bogs and in bog mountain pine stands.

Acer pseudoplatanus.d: Large maple with five-lobed, coarsely toothed leaves, no milky sap, and winged fruits set at a right angle. Flaky bark. Common in ravines, on scree and in tall-herb stands up to the treeline.

Kalmia procumbens.d: Prostrate, mat-forming dwarf shrub with tiny, leathery, opposite leaves and small pink flowers. Grows on wind-swept acidic ridges where little snow lies.

Corallorhiza trifida.d: Small, leafless, yellowish-green orchid with coral-like underground rhizomes and a few small greenish-white flowers. Grows in mossy spruce forests and damp, shady conifer woods.

Dactylorhiza fuchsii.d: Orchid with dark-spotted leaves and spikes of pale pink flowers whose three-lobed lip is marked with dark loops and dots. Grows in spruce and fir forests and in damp meadows at forest edges.

Abies alba.d: Tall conifer with flat needles carrying two white bands beneath and a notched tip; upright cones that break apart on the tree. Grey, smooth bark. Needs humid, shady slopes and pairs with spruce and beech in mixed montane forest.

Fagus sylvatica.d: Tall tree with smooth grey bark and oval, wavy-edged leaves; three-angled nuts in spiny husks. Dominates montane forests on fresh soils.

Pinus sylvestris.d: Pine with bluish, twisted paired needles and orange, flaking bark in the upper crown. Dominates dry, sunny slopes and warm inner valleys.

Anemone trifolia.d: Woodland anemone whose stem leaves are divided into three toothed leaflets; single white flower. A south-eastern Alpine species of beech and mixed fir forests.

Carex alba.d: Delicate sedge with thread-like leaves and small spikes with silvery-white bracts. Grows in dry, light pine and oak woods on limestone.

Lilium martagon.d: Tall lily with whorls of broad leaves and nodding, purple-spotted pink flowers whose petals curl back like a turban. Grows in light woods and mountain meadows.

Cardamine enneaphyllos.d: Woodland plant with whorls of three leaves, each divided into three, and nodding pale yellow flowers in spring. Grows in base-rich beech forests.

Cyclamen purpurascens.d: Low plant with round, silver-marbled leaves and fragrant pink-purple flowers with swept-back petals in late summer. Grows in beech, hop-hornbeam and mixed woods on limestone.

Epipactis helleborine.d: Orchid with broad, ribbed leaves and a long spike of greenish to purplish flowers. Common in beech and mixed woods.

Fraxinus excelsior.d: Tall tree with pinnate leaves of 9-13 toothed leaflets and velvety black buds; winged fruits hang in bunches. Grows in floodplain, ravine and lime-ash forests on fresh, rich soils.

Mercurialis perennis.d: Carpet-forming woodland herb with paired, toothed leaves and small green flowers. Indicates base-rich, fresh soils in beech and hop-hornbeam woods.

Neottia nidus-avis.d: Leafless, honey-brown orchid without chlorophyll, feeding on fungi. Grows in deep shade in beech forests.

Primula vulgaris.d: Primrose with wrinkled leaves and single pale yellow flowers on long stalks in early spring. Grows in beech woods and hedges.

Laburnum alpinum.d: Small tree with trifoliate leaves and long, hanging chains of yellow pea flowers in early summer; flat, hairless pods. All parts are poisonous. Grows in south-eastern Alpine beech woods.

Epipactis atrorubens.d: Orchid with a hairy stem and spike of wine-red, vanilla-scented flowers. Grows in light pine woods and on limestone scree.

Fraxinus ornus.d: Small tree with pinnate leaves and fragrant, creamy white flower plumes in spring. Typical of warm hop-hornbeam and oak woods.

Quercus petraea.d: Oak with long-stalked, regularly lobed leaves and stalkless acorns. Grows on warm, acidic slopes with chestnut and pine.

Sorbus aria.d: Tree with oval, toothed leaves white-felted beneath and red berries. Grows in dry, sunny woods.

Daphne cneorum.d: Low, evergreen shrublet with narrow leaves and dense heads of strongly fragrant pink flowers in late spring. Grows in light pine woods on limestone.

Goodyera repens.d: Small orchid with net-veined leaves and a spiral spike of tiny white flowers. Grows in mossy pine woods.

Ostrya carpinifolia.d: Tree with double-toothed, hornbeam-like leaves and pale, hop-like hanging fruit clusters. Dominates warm, dry hillside woods with manna ash on limestone and porphyry.

Castanea sativa.d: Tree with long, toothed, glossy leaves and spiny husks enclosing edible nuts. Grows on acidic soils of the warm lower slopes.

Celtis australis.d: Tree with smooth grey bark and asymmetric, toothed leaves; small dark berries. Grows on warm siliceous block screes.

Quercus pubescens.d: Smaller oak with leaves and young twigs covered with soft grey hairs; acorns almost stalkless. Grows on the warmest, driest slopes with manna ash and hop-hornbeam.

Ruscus aculeatus.d: Evergreen, knee-high shrub whose stiff, spine-tipped "leaves" are flattened stems; red berries sit in the middle of them. A Mediterranean plant at its northern edge in the warmest woods.

Tilia cordata.d: Tree with small, heart-shaped leaves with rusty tufts beneath and fragrant flower clusters with a wing-like bract. Grows in ravine and lime-ash forests.

Cephalanthera rubra.d: Slender orchid, 20-50 cm, with narrow leaves and a loose spike of bright pink-purple, half-open flowers in early summer. Grows in light oak, pine and beech woods on warm limestone soils.

Cephalanthera longifolia.d: Orchid with long, narrow leaves and a spike of white flowers that barely open. Grows in light, warm woods.

Cornus mas.d: Shrub or small tree that flowers before the leaves appear, covering bare twigs with small yellow clusters in late winter; edible, glossy red fruits in late summer. Grows in warm hop-hornbeam and oak woods.

Acer platanoides.d: Tree with broad, five-lobed leaves ending in fine bristle-like points; milky sap in the leaf stalk. Yellow-green flowers open before the leaves. Grows in warm ravine and lime-ash forests on fresh, nutrient-rich soils.

Alnus incana.d: Fast-growing tree with smooth grey bark and pointed, double-toothed leaves that are grey-hairy beneath. Forms woods along mountain rivers on gravelly floodplain soils.

Tilia platyphyllos.d: Tree with larger, softly hairy, heart-shaped leaves and fewer flowers per cluster than small-leaved lime. Grows in ravine forests on rich, rocky soils.

Ulmus glabra.d: Tree with large, rough, sharply double-toothed leaves with a strongly asymmetric base and winged fruits. Grows in ravine and lime-ash forests.

Salix alba.d: Large tree with narrow, silky-silvery leaves and furrowed bark. Lines rivers in the valley floors and forms floodplain woods.

Populus nigra.d: Large tree with triangular, finely toothed leaves and fissured, dark bark with burrs. Grows in alder-ash floodplain forests along major rivers.
